spec_reference: pcap-savefile(5) / the libpcap classic savefile layout as documented at https://wiki.wireshark.org/Development/LibpcapFileFormat (the reference the .bt itself cites at line 20), read against the libpcap implementation: sf-pcap.c (pcap_check_header, pcap_next_packet), savefile.c, pcap.h (PCAP_VERSION_MAJOR 2, PCAP_VERSION_MINOR 4 at lines 146-147), pcap-common.c (max_snaplen_for_dlt) and pcap-int.h (MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN). Snapshot: libpcap git master, PCAP_VERSION 2.4.

RFC 791 (Internet Protocol) for the IPv4 header: version/IHL octet, TOS, total length, identification, flags and 13-bit fragment offset, TTL, protocol, header checksum, source and destination address.
RFC 3168 / RFC 2474 for the DiffServField split into a 6-bit DSCP and 2 ECN bits.

RFC 793 (Transmission Control Protocol) for the TCP header: ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, data offset, the six control flags, window, checksum and urgent pointer, plus the options area implied by a data offset above 5.
RFC 768 (User Datagram Protocol) for the 8-octet UDP header and its optional checksum.
RFC 1071 for the one's-complement internet checksum used by both IPv4 and the transport layer.
IEEE 802.1Q (as consolidated in RFC 8100) for the 4-octet VLAN tag: 3-bit PCP, 1-bit DEI, 12-bit VID, then the inner EtherType.
IEEE 802.3 / Ethernet II for the 14-octet link header and the 60-octet minimum frame size that makes trailing padding a real thing.

IANA Protocol Numbers registry (all 256 values) and the IANA Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry, cross-checked against tcpdump's ipproto.c netdb_protocol_names[256] and its UDP/TCP port-demux tables.

The decoder whose coverage is the objective: tcpdump 5.0.0-PRE-GIT (git master snapshot), specifically print.c, print-ether.c, print-vlan.c, print-ip.c, print-ip-demux.c, print-tcp.c, print-udp.c and print-raw.c, run as 'tcpdump -nr'.
meta.structure_note: A 24-octet little-endian global header (magic, version, thiszone, sigfigs, snaplen, linktype) followed by a contiguous, self-delimiting stream of records that runs to end of file, where each record is a 16-octet little-endian header (ts_sec, ts_usec, incl_len, orig_len) and then exactly incl_len octets of big-endian frame body - optional 14-octet Ethernet header, optional 4-octet 802.1Q tag, 20-octet IPv4 header, one of three transport layouts, optional application payload, optional layer-2 padding - so the record count is the only knob on file size.
meta.constraints_note: Three things drive every tier decision in this file. (1) DERIVE, DON'T SHRINK. Every payload length in the template is an expression over other fields, never a literal: Crap[tcp_hdr_len*4-13] at line 110, packet[total_length-ip_hdr_length] at line 114, AppData[total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 - tcp_hdr_len*4] at lines 162/165 and AppData[udp_hdr_len-8] at lines 170/173, and padding[incl_len - len_before_l3 - total_length] at lines 176/177. Each of those fields is therefore recorded as a Tier A calculated_value or a Tier A payload_wellformedness with a derives_from list, and each also appears in diversity_axes. The generator picks the ports, the flags, the protocol and the payload shape first and then sizes total_length, udp_hdr_len, incl_len, orig_len, snaplen and HdrChecksum around them. Nothing was narrowed to make a fixed payload fit. (2) ONE SIZE KNOB, AND IT IS NOT A FIELD. The only repeat-controlling construct is while(!FEof()) at lines 217-220, so the record count lives in structure.output_budget on the 'PCAPRECORD stream' and 'PCAPRECORD' entries. No dimension, count or length field carries a generation range, a practical bound, or a narrowed value set anywhere in this file; the 14 Tier C fields are declared unconstrained precisely so that MAC octets, IP octets, TTL, DSCP, identification, sequence and acknowledgement numbers and both timestamp words stay free. (3) THE GATE IS THE HEADER, NOT THE CONTENT. libpcap's pcap_check_header (sf-pcap.c:218-470) and pcap_next_packet (sf-pcap.c:492-760) are the only places a file is rejected outright: a bad magic, a bad major version, a minor version above 4, set reserved bits in the linktype word, a caplen above MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN, or a caplen that runs past end of file. Once a record is delivered, tcpdump essentially never refuses it - it prints '[|proto]' or '[bad ...]' and moves on - so almost every frame field is free or enumerable rather than pinned, and the value is in choosing values that route the printer somewhere deep.

schema_extensions.name: valid_values written as an inclusive-range object
schema_extensions.why: Both fields are 16 bits and every value 0..65535 is a legal port, so an exhaustive valid_values array is 65536 integers - twice, ~0.8 MB and ~131k lines of bare numbers that no consumer can read and that carry no information beyond the domain width. The object form {"form": "inclusive_integer_range", "min": 0, "max": 65535, "count": 65536, "meaning": ...} states the same exhaustive set unambiguously and cannot be misread as a two-value enumeration. This is not a narrowing: the values worth favouring are listed separately in preferred_value.

schema_extensions.name: value_names as prose class descriptions rather than one name per value
schema_extensions.why: The documented use is a parallel array to valid_values where the enum has real names. Ports, fragment offsets, header lengths and reserved nibbles have no per-value names, so value_names instead groups the domain into the classes that behave differently in the decoder and names the printer each class reaches. Layer_3.L4proto keeps the strict parallel form: 256 values, 256 IANA names.

schema_extensions.name: payload_wellformedness entries that also carry the calculated_value keys
schema_extensions.why: These three fields are simultaneously a length-derived array (the .bt sizes them from other fields, so the rewrite must backpatch) and an encoded stream (their bytes must form a real transport or application message, so the rewrite must emit one). Recording only one half would lose either the size arithmetic or the codec recipe, so each entry carries codec / must_produce / decoder_gate / generation_strategy / derives_from / content_is_free AND algorithm / covers / includes_self / endianness / depends_on. The type stays payload_wellformedness, which the prompt calls the highest-value entry type.

schema_extensions.name: dependencies[].when and dependencies[].then as prose strings
schema_extensions.why: The documented shape is {"field": ..., "equals": ...}. Most of these rules are not single-field equalities: they turn on a whole-file byte order, on a value being outside a set, on two fields moving together, or on a bit inside an opaque array (the TCP control-flags octet lives inside Layer_4.Crap, which the template declares as one BYTE[]). Forcing them into field/equals objects would distort or drop them, so when/then stay prose and the machine-checkable part is carried by the constraint entries they reference. Every entry still has the documented description, source and confidence keys.

schema_extensions.name: structure[] extra keys: name, starts_at, length, repeat, until, notes
schema_extensions.why: rule / subject / detail / condition / description / source / output_budget / generation_note are all present as documented. The additions carry what a generator of a self-delimiting record stream needs and the documented keys have no home for: the byte offset each section starts at, its exact octet count or the expression yielding it, its cardinality, and what terminates the repetition. detail is composed from length, repeat and until, so no fact is stated only in an extension key.

source_evidence.settled: The only place a pcap file is refused outright. pcap_check_header (218-470): the magic test and its byte-order/swap decision (238-247), the major-version test, the minor-version > 4 rejection, and the reserved-bits test on the linktype word (300-303) - these four make magic_number, version_major, version_minor and network Tier A. pcap_next_packet (492-760): the 4-octet record-header read that fixes ts_sec's width against the .bt's time_t, the caplen/len exchange for version_minor (564-583), the hard error for caplen above MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN (589-608), and the snapshot clamping / bytes_to_discard / truncated-record path (611-712) that makes snaplen and incl_len a real axis rather than a cosmetic one.

pcapint_adjust_snapshot in savefile.c substitutes max_snaplen_for_dlt(linktype) for a snaplen of 0 or above INT_MAX, which is why snaplen 0 is safe; pcap.h:146-147 gives PCAP_VERSION_MAJOR 2 / PCAP_VERSION_MINOR 4 and bounds version_minor; pcap-int.h gives MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN; pcap-common.c gives the linktype table behind network 1 (LINKTYPE_ETHERNET) and 101 (LINKTYPE_RAW); netdissect.h gives the ND_ICHECKMSG_* macros whose text appears in the decoder_gate strings.

The link-layer dispatch that PCAPHEADER.network selects: print.c:85 maps DLT_EN10MB to ether_if_print, print.c:206 maps DLT_RAW to raw_if_print, print.c:299 is unsupported_if_print. print-ether.c's ether_common_print does the EtherType dispatch, the 0x8100/0x88a8/0x9100/0x9200 recursion into print-vlan.c, and the llc_print fallback for values <= 1500 - which is what makes Layer_2.L3type and Dot1q.L3type diversity axes rather than free text.

Every Tier A decision in the IPv4 header: the version test at 341, the header-length test at 343-344 (hlen < 20 -> invalid), the total_length-versus-captured-length warning at 346-350, the length < hlen test at 362, the TTL print at 413, the DF/MF bittok2str at 418, and above all the fragment-offset gate at 469 'if ((off & IP_OFFMASK) == 0)' whose else branch (496-517) prints 'ip-proto-%u' and returns - the reason Layer_3.Flags is Tier A.

ip_demux_print, the protocol-number switch that Layer_3.L4proto selects, cited once per protocol in the L4PROTO_RECIPES table - hence its very high citation count. It is what makes all 256 L4proto values worth keeping and what the per-protocol generation_strategy recipes are built for. ipproto.c's netdb_protocol_names[256] supplied the value_names of the L4proto entry and was cross-checked against the IANA Protocol Numbers registry.

The TCP half of the transport layer. tcp.h:53-54 tcp_get_flags() is '(GET_U_1(th_flags) | ((GET_U_1(th_offx2) & 0x0f) << 8))', which is the only reason Layer_4.Reserved is Tier B rather than Tier C - bit 8 of the flags word is TH_AE (Accurate ECN) and print-tcp.c:114 prints it as 'e'. print-tcp.c:749-750 'if (length == 0) return;' is the gate that makes a zero-length TCP payload delete the entire port demux at 788-872; 759-763 re-derives the payload length exactly as line 162 of the .bt does; 421 gates checksum verification on 'fragmented' and ndo_vflag; 257/271/275 cover th_seq, the flags string and the relative-sequence bookkeeping. The port-demux table itself was extracted from every IS_SRC_OR_DST_PORT / IS_SRC_OR_DST_PORT_RANGE macro and every bare dport== / sport== comparison in the file.

The UDP half. 380-386 applies ND_ICHECKMSG_ZU("undersized-udplength", ulen, <, sizeof(struct udphdr)) and then clamps with 'if (ulen < length) length = ulen;', which is why Layer_4.udp_hdr_len is Tier A calculated_value and why a udp_hdr_len of 8 silently hands the demuxed printer zero bytes; 504 is the verbose-only checksum gate; 560-700 is the port demux whose entries became UDP_RECIPES.

Cited from the L4PROTO_RECIPES entry for protocol 112 (VRRP) and from the Layer_4.packet generation_strategy, to state what a minimal version/type/ advertisement message looks like so that the opaque payload actually reaches a per-message switch instead of printing 'ip-proto-112'. Representative of the ~40 protocol-specific printers consulted while building the recipe tables; the recipes name the printer and the octets, and print-ip-demux.c is cited for the dispatch.

source_evidence.implementation: 010 Editor binary-template language (bt.h / the 010 Editor template reference)
source_evidence.settled: The semantics the tier decisions depend on but that no RFC states: that a struct-level if/else emits octets for exactly one branch; that <size=N> fixes a struct's octet count; that BigEndian()/LittleEndian() switch the read order from that point on, so lines 141 and 179 make the record header little-endian and the frame body big-endian; that a first-declared bitfield takes the high bits of its octet; that local variables emit no octets; and that read=/comment= callbacks are display-only and therefore never constraints.

meta.decoder: tcpdump 5.0.0-PRE-GIT (git master) reading a file written to the libpcap classic savefile layout by libpcap git master at PCAP_VERSION 2.4, invoked as 'tcpdump -nr <file>'. The -n matters: it sets ndo_nflag, which is why print-ip.c:513's netdb_protoname lookup is unreachable and a non-zero fragment offset prints 'ip-proto-%u' rather than a protocol name, and why the port demux prints numbers rather than service names. The -r matters: reading a savefile goes through sf-pcap.c's pcap_check_header and pcap_next_packet, which are the only two functions in the whole path that can refuse the file. Verbose-only branches (the IPv4 checksum recomputation at print-tcp.c:421 and print-udp.c:504, the TTL and DF/MF prints) are recorded as reachable under -v but are not the coverage target.
meta.confidence_summary: Distribution over the 107 entries: constraints high 40; dependencies high 25, medium 2; structure unstated 13; diversity_axes unstated 27. Every one of the 40 constraints is high confidence, and that is not optimism - it reflects how each tier was decided. A constraint is recorded high only when both halves are checkable: the template half is a literal line of pcap-orig.bt whose snippet is copied verbatim into evidence, and the decoder half is either a named libpcap/tcpdump test at a cited file and line, or a numbered clause of RFC 791 / 793 / 768 / 1071 / 8100 / 826. Nothing here rests on an unverifiable judgement about what a decoder 'probably' does. The two dependencies that are only medium are the two whose decoder half is a printer's behaviour rather than a gate: 'Layer_3.L4proto == 112 (VRRP) or 112-with-version-3 (CARP shares the printer path)'; and 'more than one record uses the same Layer_3.Identification together with the more-fragments bit'. Both would move to high by running generated files through 'tcpdump -nr' and diffing the output against the prediction, which is a build-time check the rewrite step can perform; neither is load-bearing for reaching deep parsing, because both describe extra output on an already-decoded packet rather than a branch that must be taken. The structure rules and diversity axes carry no confidence key in the documented schema; where they state a fact it is the same fact as a cited constraint entry, so they inherit that entry's confidence.

recorded_deviations.rule: EVERY length, size, count, offset, CRC, checksum or Adler field is a Tier A calculated_value.
recorded_deviations.deviation: Followed, including for PCAPRECORD.padding, which was first recorded as Tier B on the argument that the AMOUNT of padding is a free enumerated choice. It is Tier A: its length is the expression at line 177, and if it disagrees with incl_len the record ends at the wrong file offset, every following header is misaligned, and the decoder stops doing useful work. The freedom is real but belongs to PCAPRECORD.incl_len, which is where it is recorded (Tier A calculated_value, listed in diversity_axes with must_remain_unconstrained true).

recorded_deviations.rule: If this format has no compressed or encoded payload, say so explicitly in meta.structure_note.
recorded_deviations.deviation: The negative case does not arise: there are three payload_wellformedness entries (Layer_4.Crap, Layer_4.packet, PCAPRECORD.AppData) and structure_note describes them. What is recorded instead is that none is a compression codec - the 'encoding' is transport and application framing, not zlib or LZW - so there is no stored-block or clear-code shortcut of the kind the prompt recommends. The equivalent here is the minimal legal message named in each entry's generation_strategy, which gets the demuxed printer all the way in.

recorded_deviations.rule: EVERY typedef enum is a Tier B enumerated_values entry with "completeness": "exhaustive", or a stated reason why not.
recorded_deviations.deviation: Satisfied vacuously, and stated as such: pcap-orig.bt declares no enum and no enum-typed field. The nearest things are integer fields whose meaning is a registry lookup - Layer_3.L4proto against the IANA Protocol Numbers registry (256 values, all legal, Tier B enumerated_values, completeness exhaustive, 256-entry value_names) and PCAPHEADER.network against the DLT registry (Tier A bitmask_constraint rather than enumerated_values, because the template can only serialise two of the accepted values and the reason is in that entry's notes).

recorded_deviations.rule: EVERY dimension, count and repeat-controlling field appears as a Tier C entry with "type": "unconstrained", and also in diversity_axes.
recorded_deviations.deviation: Four Tier C fields are deliberately absent from diversity_axes: PCAPHEADER.thiszone, PCAPHEADER.sigfigs, Dot1q.priority and Dot1q.dei. None is a dimension, a count or repeat-controlling, none is a field a size-conscious author would be tempted to pin, and none drives the decoder down a different path: thiszone and sigfigs are copied through by sf-pcap.c and never read again, and priority and dei are printed but never switched on. All four remain full Tier C unconstrained entries in constraints, which is where a generator gets their domains. diversity_axes is documented as the fields whose variation drives decoder behaviour, and Dot1q.id is listed there with the priority/dei relationship stated in its entry.

recorded_deviations.rule: Every field in any payload_wellformedness.derives_from also appears in diversity_axes with must_remain_unconstrained: true.
recorded_deviations.deviation: All eight derives_from fields do appear in diversity_axes. Seven carry must_remain_unconstrained true. The eighth, Layer_3.ip_hdr_len, carries false, because its only template-consistent value is 5 - the IPv4 branch emits a fixed 20-octet header with no options array, so 6..15 desynchronise every length expression built from it - and claiming the field must remain unconstrained would contradict its own Tier A constraint entry. The rule's intent - never narrow a field to suit the payload it sizes - is honoured instead by the derive-don't-shrink statement in meta.constraints_note and by that axis entry's own explanation. For the Tier A length fields, must_remain_unconstrained means 'do not narrow further', not 'emit any value': they vary only through the fields they are calculated from, which is exactly what the rule protects.

tier_counts.note: Tier A entries are the ones a conforming libpcap refuses the file over, or that stop tcpdump before it dissects anything: the magic, both version fields, the reserved bits of the linktype word, every length and every checksum, the four-octet width of ts_sec against the .bt's time_t declaration, and the fragment-offset gate. Tier B entries are complete domains that decide how deep parsing goes - all 256 protocol numbers, all 65536 ports, all sixteen reserved nibbles, the four usable flag combinations. Tier C entries carry no value set, no minimum and no maximum at all, which is what makes this file safe to hand to a generator that would otherwise cap a dimension to keep files small.

coverage_axes_summary.payoff: The largest single multiplier in the format: one octet selects among roughly forty protocol printers through ip_demux_print, and all 256 values are legal. It also decides whether Layer_4 is TCP or UDP at all, and therefore which of the two port demuxes can run.

The second multiplier: print-tcp.c:788-872 and print-udp.c:560-700 together demux on the order of a hundred application printers by port value. Reaching any of them additionally requires a non-zero payload length, so this axis only pays when PCAPRECORD.AppData is emitted with real bytes inside it - the 'if (length == 0) return;' at print-tcp.c:749-750 is what deletes the whole demux otherwise.

The format's only size knob, and the only way to make one file exercise many combinations of every other axis. Zero records is legal and the count is unbounded above; libpcap re-enters pcap_next_packet per record with no cross-record state but the file offset, which makes a multi-record file the cheapest coverage available.

Selects the link layer: 1 (DLT_EN10MB) gives an Ethernet header and an EtherType dispatch through print.c:85, 101 (DLT_RAW) gives a bare IP datagram through print.c:206 with no link layer at all. Two disjoint decode trees from one 32-bit field, and the only two this template can serialise.

0x0800 reaches IPv4, 0x8100/0x88a8/0x9100/0x9200 recurse into print-vlan.c before it, and any value <= 1500 falls into llc_print instead - a third link-layer path. The template makes only 0x0800 and 0x8100 serialisable, so the LLC path is decoder-side coverage this template cannot emit, which is recorded rather than pretended away.

Cheap and brutal: a non-zero fragment offset makes print-ip.c:469's 'if ((off & IP_OFFMASK) == 0)' take its else branch, print 'ip-proto-%u' and return, deleting the entire transport demux. The four combinations 0x0000/0x2000/0x4000/0x6000 are the Tier B domain and each yields visibly different output, including the -v DF/MF rendering at print-ip.c:418.

0 through 4 are all accepted, and sf-pcap.c:564-583 exchanges caplen and len for the older minor versions, so the same bytes mean different things. It is the only header field besides the magic that changes how every record in the file is interpreted.

The truncation axis, and the one most likely to be silently capped by a size-conscious rewrite. total_length larger than what was captured produces print-ip.c:347's '[total length %u > length %u]' warning; incl_len larger than the frame body produces padding and the same warning from the other direction; incl_len smaller makes libpcap report a short record. All three are derived, so the real knob is the AppData size the generator chooses.

Drives the clamping, bytes_to_discard and truncated-record path in pcap_next_packet (611-712) and the hard error above MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN (589-608). A snaplen of 0 is safe rather than degenerate because pcapint_adjust_snapshot substitutes max_snaplen_for_dlt(linktype).

A data offset above 5 puts option octets inside Layer_4.Crap and changes what the transport printers see, without changing anything the template sizes independently. Reserved is the one nibble in the file where a value is actually read: its low bit is TH_AE (Accurate ECN), folded into the flags word by tcp.h:53-54's tcp_get_flags and printed as 'e', which is why the nibble is Tier B over all sixteen values with preferred_value [0, 1] rather than Tier C.

Free entropy with real decoder paths behind it: the MAC name lookup, the broadcast/multicast cases, and the address-rendering branch that -n suppresses. Worth varying because they cost nothing and every octet is already in the file.

Reachable only when network == 1 and Layer_2.L3type == 0x8100, so it pays only in combination with axes 4 and 5. id 0 and 4095 are the reserved endpoints of the 12-bit domain; priority and dei are printed but never switched on, which is why they are Tier C and not listed as separate axes.

coverage_axes_summary.field: PCAPRECORD.ts_sec / ts_usec, Layer_3.Identification, Layer_3.TTL, Layer_3.DiffServField, Layer_4.SEQ, Layer_4.ACK
coverage_axes_summary.payoff: Lowest payoff per octet: formatted, compared or accumulated, but never used to choose a branch. They are Tier C precisely because no value is more productive than another, and they are still worth varying so successive files are not near-identical. ts_sec carries the single hard requirement in this group - exactly four octets on the wire, never the eight its time_t declaration implies on a 64-bit host.

PCAPHEADER.magic_number.tier_rationale: libpcap's pcap_check_header() (sf-pcap.c:239-249) compares the first four bytes, byte-swapped as well as not, against TCPDUMP_MAGIC / KUZNETZOV_TCPDUMP_MAGIC / NSEC_TCPDUMP_MAGIC and returns NULL with "bad dump file magic number" on a miss, so tcpdump prints "tcpdump: <file>: not a pcap file" and dissects nothing at all; the template itself also stops at lines 25-27.
PCAPHEADER.magic_number.description: Four-byte pcap savefile magic identifying byte order and timestamp resolution; must be 0xa1b2c3d4 for a little-endian, microsecond-resolution classic pcap file.
PCAPHEADER.magic_number.notes: Read under the LittleEndian() in force from line 214, so the on-disk bytes are D4 C3 B2 A1 (matching the 'ID Bytes' comment at line 11). libpcap also accepts 0xa1b2cd34 (KUZNETZOV_TCPDUMP_MAGIC, sf-pcap.c:76) and 0xa1b23c4d (NSEC_TCPDUMP_MAGIC, nanosecond timestamps, sf-pcap.c:94), in either byte order. Line 25's guard admits only 0xA1B2C3D4, so the rewrite must widen it if the nanosecond or Kuznetsov variants are wanted; NSEC_TCPDUMP_MAGIC additionally makes libpcap scale ts_usec (sf-pcap.c:560-565) and changes tcpdump's timestamp printing.

PCAPHEADER.version_major.tier_rationale: sf-pcap.c:286-292 refuses the whole file with "unsupported pcap savefile version %d.%d" unless (version_major == 2 && version_minor <= 4) or (version_major == 543 && version_minor == 0), so any other value stops tcpdump before it reads a single record.
PCAPHEADER.version_major.description: Major version of the pcap savefile format; only 2 (and the DG/UX oddity 543) is accepted by libpcap.
PCAPHEADER.version_major.notes: PCAP_VERSION_MAJOR == 2 (libpcap pcap.h:146). version_major == 543 with version_minor == 0 is also accepted and forces the pre-2.3 (swapped) caplen/len order (sf-pcap.c:389-405), but the record layout below assumes the 2.x field order, so 2 is the value to emit.

PCAPHEADER.version_minor.tier_rationale: A wrong value does not make the decoder refuse the file for every legal choice: sf-pcap.c:286 accepts any version_minor <= 4 when version_major == 2, and each accepted value merely selects a different branch of the lengths_swapped switch at sf-pcap.c:389-400, so the legal set is finite and enumerable rather than pinned.
PCAPHEADER.version_minor.description: Minor pcap savefile version; 0..4 are all accepted by libpcap and select how the per-record caplen/len pair is interpreted.
value_names: 2.0 - pre-2.3 layout: libpcap sets lengths_swapped = SWAPPED and always exchanges caplen/len after reading them
2.1 - pre-2.3 layout: lengths_swapped = SWAPPED
2.2 - pre-2.3 layout: lengths_swapped = SWAPPED
2.3 - transitional: lengths_swapped = MAYBE_SWAPPED; libpcap exchanges the pair only if the first field read is greater than the second
2.4 - current: lengths_swapped = NOT_SWAPPED; the pair is read as (incl_len, orig_len)
PCAPHEADER.version_minor.completeness_rationale: PCAP_VERSION_MINOR == 4 (pcap.h:147) and sf-pcap.c:287 requires version_minor <= PCAP_VERSION_MINOR, so 5..65535 are refused with "unsupported pcap savefile version".
PCAPHEADER.version_minor.notes: 0, 1 and 2 are genuine distinct branches and must stay in valid_values, but they are only usable if the record header is emitted in the pre-2.3 order (orig_len first, then incl_len) - see the two dependencies on this field. 3 is safe with the normal order as long as incl_len <= orig_len, which the orig_len gate already guarantees. 4 is the only value with no reordering caveat, hence preferred.

PCAPHEADER.thiszone.tier_rationale: No decoder reads it: libpcap reads it into the header struct and discards it, and tcpdump never consults it, timestamps being printed straight from ts_sec/ts_usec, so pinning it to 0 would cost a free 32-bit word for zero coverage.
PCAPHEADER.thiszone.description: GMT-to-local correction in seconds; documented as "SHOULD be filled with 0" by pcap-savefile(5) but never validated or used by libpcap or tcpdump.

evidence.snippet: int32  thiszone;       /* GMT to local correction */
evidence.note: The line and snippet anchor the field in the template; the claim that nothing constrains its value is spec-side negative evidence. sf-pcap.c:255-266 reads thiszone into the header struct and never tests it, savefile.c never consults it, and tcpdump prints timestamps straight from the record header's ts_sec/ts_usec (print.c), so no printer ever looks at it. pcap-savefile(5) and the libpcap wiki both say it SHOULD be 0 - advice, not a check.

PCAPHEADER.thiszone.notes: Listed precisely because pcap-savefile(5) and the libpcap wiki both say it "SHOULD be 0", which invites a pin. It is SHOULD, not MUST: sf-pcap.c:255-266 reads the field and never tests it. Leave it free.

PCAPHEADER.sigfigs.tier_rationale: Reserved field nobody checks: sf-pcap.c reads it and never tests it and tcpdump never reads it, so any value is accepted and constraining it only removes a free word.
PCAPHEADER.sigfigs.description: Accuracy of timestamps, reserved; pcap-savefile(5) says it "SHOULD be filled with 0" but no decoder validates it.

evidence.note: The line and snippet anchor the field in the template; the claim that nothing constrains its value is spec-side negative evidence. sf-pcap.c reads sigfigs into the header struct in the same block as thiszone (255-266) and never tests it, savefile.c never consults it, and no tcpdump printer refers to it. pcap-savefile(5) documents it as reserved and says it SHOULD be 0 - advice, not a check.

PCAPHEADER.sigfigs.notes: The rule 'reserved fields nobody checks -> Tier C' applies exactly. Do not pin to 0.

PCAPHEADER.snaplen.tier_rationale: A wrong value stops the decoder before it does useful work on every record: sf-pcap.c:611-700 truncates any record whose incl_len exceeds p->snapshot to exactly p->snapshot bytes and discards the remainder, so a snaplen smaller than the largest incl_len silently amputates the packet payload tcpdump would otherwise dissect.
PCAPHEADER.snaplen.description: Maximum number of octets captured per packet; must be 0 or at least the largest incl_len in the file.

evidence.snippet: uint32 snaplen;        /* max length of captured packets, in octets */

PCAPHEADER.snaplen.algorithm: snaplen = 0, OR snaplen = max(PCAPRECORD.incl_len) over every record in the file. 0 is a free and fully valid choice: savefile.c:439-454 pcapint_adjust_snapshot() substitutes max_snaplen_for_dlt(linktype), which is MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN (262144, pcap-int.h:158) for DLT_EN10MB and DLT_RAW, so no record is ever truncated. Values greater than INT_MAX are substituted the same way. The only harmful region is 1 .. (max incl_len - 1).
PCAPHEADER.snaplen.covers: No bytes of the file itself; it is an upper bound on every PCAPRECORD.incl_len that follows.
PCAPHEADER.snaplen.notes: snaplen is not a hard gate: exceeding it causes truncation, not an error return. It is Tier A because that truncation is exactly 'stopping before doing useful work' for the discarded bytes. Emitting 0 is the simplest always-correct choice and additionally exercises the snaplen == 0 branch of pcapint_adjust_snapshot().

PCAPHEADER.network.tier_rationale: Bits 16-25 are a reserved field libpcap validates for the whole file: sf-pcap.c:300-306 returns NULL with "savefile linktype reserved field not zero (0x%08x)" whenever LT_RESERVED1(linktype) != 0, so one evil bit there costs every record in the file, not one.
PCAPHEADER.network.description: 32-bit link-layer type field: a 16-bit LINKTYPE_ value in bits 0-15, a reserved field in bits 16-25 that must be zero, and optional FCS metadata in bits 26-31.
PCAPHEADER.network.valid_bits: 0x0000FFFF = LT_LINKTYPE(x), the LINKTYPE_ value that selects tcpdump's link-layer printer (pcap.h:265). 0x03FF0000 = LT_RESERVED1(x), which MUST be zero (pcap.h:267; enforced at sf-pcap.c:300). 0xFFFF0000 = LT_LINKTYPE_EXT(x) (pcap.h:266); within it bits 26-27 carry LT_FCS_LENGTH and bit 28 the LT_FCS_NOT_PRESENT flag. Emitting zero across the whole upper half is the only safe construction.
value_names: 1 = LINKTYPE_ETHERNET (DLT_EN10MB) - Ethernet II, 14-byte link header; tcpdump print.c:85 maps it to ether_if_print
101 = LINKTYPE_RAW (DLT_RAW) - bare IPv4/IPv6 with no link header; tcpdump print.c:206 maps it to raw_if_print
PCAPHEADER.network.completeness_rationale: the LINKTYPE registry defines about 280 values and libpcap accepts any of them with the reserved bits clear, but this template can only produce a self-consistent file for 1 and 101. Line 144 branches on exactly two cases: network == 101 emits no link header at all, and every other value emits the 14-byte Layer_2 header (optionally plus a 4-byte Dot1q). A LINKTYPE whose tcpdump printer expects a different link-header size - 0/LINKTYPE_NULL (4-byte AF header), 9/LINKTYPE_PPP (0 or 2 bytes), 113/LINKTYPE_LINUX_SLL (16 bytes), 228/LINKTYPE_IPV4 (0 bytes) - would make tcpdump misread the bytes the template wrote. Values with no printer at all fall through to unsupported_if_print() at print.c:299, which prints nothing of the packet. Widening this set requires the rewrite to add the corresponding link-layer layouts, not merely more enum values.
PCAPHEADER.network.notes: Both values must be emitted: they take completely different paths in the template (line 144 versus line 146) and in tcpdump (ether_if_print -> ether_common_print -> 802.1Q recursion -> EtherType dispatch, versus raw_if_print -> ip_print directly). This is the largest structural switch in the format. value_names, completeness and preferred_value are carried on this bitmask_constraint entry as a recorded schema extension; the base schema lists them under enumerated_values.

MACaddr.Byte.tier_rationale: Neither libpcap nor tcpdump validates a MAC address in any way - print-ether.c only formats the six bytes with mac48_string() - so any value yields a file that is processed identically, and pinning addresses would remove two 48-bit diversity words per frame.
MACaddr.Byte.description: One octet of a 48-bit IEEE 802 MAC-48 address; this struct is instantiated twice per Ethernet frame as Layer_2.DstMac and Layer_2.SrcMac.
MACaddr.Byte.notes: Free in every bit, including the I/G bit (Byte[0] & 0x01) and the U/L bit (Byte[0] & 0x02). Broadcast (ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff), multicast and locally-administered addresses are all legal and all print identically under 'tcpdump -nr' (addresses are shown only with -e). Varying them costs nothing and keeps frames distinguishable.

Layer_2.L3type.tier_rationale: A wrong value does not make the decoder refuse the file: tcpdump's ether_common_print dispatches on any 16-bit length/type value, treating <= 1500 as an IEEE 802.3 length and > 1500 as an EtherType, so the legal set is finite and enumerable rather than pinned.
Layer_2.L3type.description: Ethernet II EtherType selecting the network-layer protocol that follows the 14-byte link header; this template can only build a Layer_3 for IPv4 and for the 802.1Q tag that precedes it.
value_names: 0x0800 = ETHERTYPE_IP - IPv4; line 150 instantiates Layer_3 directly after the link header
0x8100 = ETHERTYPE_8021Q - VLAN tag; line 153 inserts a 4-byte Dot1q before Layer_3
Layer_2.L3type.completeness_rationale: and the reason is the template, not the format. Lines 149-156 handle only 0x0800 and 0x8100; for any other value neither branch fires, no L3 object is ever constructed, and line 158 'Layer_4 L4(L3.ip_hdr_len,L3.total_length,L3.L4proto)' dereferences an undeclared L3, so the template's own parse fails and the generator cannot emit the record. tcpdump itself would happily dispatch 0x0806 (ARP), 0x86DD (IPv6), 0x8035 (RARP), 0x88CC (LLDP), 0x88E5 (MACsec), the Q-in-Q tags 0x88A8/0x9100/0x9200, and any value <= 1500 to llc_print. Adding those requires a matching Layer_3 variant per EtherType in the rewrite.
Layer_2.L3type.notes: Both values must be emitted: 0x8100 adds four bytes to len_before_l3 (line 154), which changes every downstream length, and makes tcpdump recurse through its 802.1Q tag printer before reaching the EtherType dispatch. Both legal values are > 1500, so the IEEE 802.3 length/LLC path in ether_common_print is never taken by this template.

Dot1q.priority.tier_rationale: A 3-bit PCP field no decoder validates; tcpdump prints it only under -v and 'tcpdump -nr' ignores it entirely, so pinning it would delete three free bits per tagged frame.
Dot1q.priority.description: Priority Code Point, the upper three bits of the 802.1Q tag control information; any value 0..7 is legal.

evidence.note: The line and snippet anchor the bitfield in the template; the claim that nothing constrains its value is spec-side negative evidence. print-vlan.c's vlan_print reads the 16-bit TCI only to print it and only under -v, so the 'tcpdump -nr' invocation this specification targets never looks at PCP; libpcap never inspects it at all. IEEE 802.1Q clause 9.6 assigns 0..7 with no reserved value.

Dot1q.priority.notes: IEEE 802.1Q clause 9.6. Together with dei and id it forms the 16-bit TCI; the .bt splits one uint16 across three bitfields (lines 51-53), which is the correct big-endian layout.

Dot1q.dei.tier_rationale: A 1-bit Drop Eligible Indicator no decoder validates and 'tcpdump -nr' never prints; constraining it would remove a free bit for nothing.
Dot1q.dei.description: Drop Eligible Indicator, bit 12 of the 802.1Q TCI (formerly the CFI bit); either value is legal.

evidence.note: The line and snippet anchor the bitfield in the template; the claim that nothing constrains its value is spec-side negative evidence. print-vlan.c prints this bit as 'DEI' only under -v and never tests it; libpcap's link-layer dispatch on 0x8100 does not look at the TCI at all. Both historical readings of the bit - Canonically Format Indicator in 802.1Q-2005 and Drop Eligible Indicator in 802.1Q-2011 - accept 0 and 1.

Dot1q.dei.notes: Was Canonically Format Indicator in 802.1Q-2005 and became Drop Eligible Indicator in 802.1Q-2011; tcpdump prints it as 'DEI' under -v. Both historical meanings accept 0 and 1.

Dot1q.id.tier_rationale: A 12-bit VLAN identifier with 4096 encodable values, none of which any decoder validates; narrowing it would collapse a free 12-bit axis to buy no depth.
Dot1q.id.description: VLAN Identifier (VID), the low 12 bits of the 802.1Q TCI; 0 means priority-tagged with no VLAN and 4095 is reserved by the standard, but every value parses.

evidence.note: The line and snippet anchor the bitfield in the template; the claim that nothing constrains its value is spec-side negative evidence. print-vlan.c prints the VID only under -v and never tests it, and libpcap's 0x8100 dispatch in print-ether.c recurses into vlan_print without reading the TCI, so no decoder path validates the VID. IEEE 802.1Q reserves 0 (priority-tagged, no VLAN) and 4095, but a frame carrying either still parses and still prints.

Dot1q.id.notes: A dimension-like field a size-conscious author might be tempted to restrict to 1..4094; the decoder does not care, so leave it free.

Dot1q.L3type.tier_rationale: Tier A by template necessity rather than decoder refusal: line 155 binds d1q.L3type to Layer_3's proto_type parameter, and only proto_type == 0x0800 (line 75) declares the Identification/Flags/TTL/L4proto/HdrChecksum/SRC_IP/DST_IP members that line 158 unconditionally dereferences, so any other value makes the .bt's own parse fail and the generator cannot emit the record at all.
Dot1q.L3type.description: EtherType inside an 802.1Q tag; must be 0x0800 (IPv4) for this template, because that is the only inner protocol for which Layer_3 declares the IPv4 member set.
Dot1q.L3type.notes: tcpdump itself accepts any inner EtherType and recurses through ether_common_print's 'recurse:' label, including nested tags. If the rewrite adds non-IPv4 Layer_3 handling this pin becomes Tier B with the same value set as Layer_2.L3type minus 0x8100, and Q-in-Q nesting becomes a further axis. Recorded as a close call: the tier is driven by what the template can express, not by what the format permits.

IPv4addr.Byte.tier_rationale: tcpdump only formats these four octets with GET_IPADDR_STRING and never validates them, and the .bt's IPv4addrName() (lines 62-67) merely sprintf's them, so every one of the 2^32 addresses per field yields an identically-processed file.
IPv4addr.Byte.description: One octet of a 32-bit IPv4 address in network byte order; this struct is instantiated twice per IPv4 datagram as Layer_3.SRC_IP and Layer_3.DST_IP.
IPv4addr.Byte.notes: Free in every octet, including the special-use ranges: 0.0.0.0/8, 127.0.0.0/8 loopback, 169.254.0.0/16 link-local, 224.0.0.0/4 multicast, 240.0.0.0/4 reserved, 255.255.255.255 broadcast. A multicast destination is the one value that can change control flow beyond printing, since tcpdump's IGMP and mtrace printers key off the destination group, so it is worth including in the mix without being required.

Layer_3.version.tier_rationale: tcpdump's ip4_print rejects the datagram outright: print-ip.c:341 is ND_ICHECKMSG_U("version", IP_V(ip), !=, 4), which expands (netdissect.h:422-428) to printing " [version %u != 4]" and 'goto invalid', whose label calls nd_print_invalid() and returns without dissecting anything below the IP header.
Layer_3.version.description: Upper nibble of the first IP octet; the IP version, which must be 4 for this template's IPv4 Layer_3.
Layer_3.version.required_value_ascii: 0x4 in the high nibble of the octet shared with ip_hdr_len
Layer_3.version.notes: The nibble shares one octet with ip_hdr_len, so the on-disk byte is (version << 4) | ip_hdr_len; with version = 4 the byte is 0x45 .. 0x4F. RFC 791 section 3.1. The value 6 would select the IPv6 printer, which this template cannot produce because lines 75-88 only declare IPv4 members; a version-6 byte here makes Layer_3 fall to the 'else' branch at line 87 and emit an Unknown[] blob, after which tcpdump still reports " [version 6 != 4] (invalid)".

Layer_3.ip_hdr_len.tier_rationale: Two independent hard gates, and they agree on one value. In the decoder, print-ip.c:343-344 computes hlen = IP_HL(ip) * 4 and applies ND_ICHECKMSG_ZU("header length", hlen, <, sizeof (struct ip)), printing " [header length %u < 20]" and 'goto invalid' for any value below 5. In the template, the IPv4 branch at lines 75-84 emits exactly 20 header octets and no options array - line 87's Unknown[hdr_length-4] lives in the else branch for proto_type != 0x0800 - so any ip_hdr_len above 5 makes line 93's ip_hdr_length = VER_HDR*4 disagree with the octets actually written by 4 per extra word, shifting the transport header, line 114's packet[], line 162's AppDataLen and line 177's padding alike.
Layer_3.ip_hdr_len.description: Lower nibble of the first IP octet: the IP header length in 32-bit words. Must be 5..15, and must equal the true header length so that tcpdump finds the transport header where the template put it.
Layer_3.ip_hdr_len.valid_bits: All four bits are the value; there is no reserved sub-field. The field is the low nibble of the octet whose high nibble is version, so the octet is (version << 4) | ip_hdr_len.
value_names: 5 = 20-byte header with no options; the overwhelmingly common case and the value every downstream length expression is calibrated for

6..15 = 24..60-byte header carrying IP options (RFC 791 section 3.1). Legal on the wire and parsed by tcpdump's -v option walk, but NOT reachable through this template's IPv4 path: lines 75-84 emit a fixed 20-octet header with no options array, so declaring 6..15 desynchronises every length expression that multiplies ip_hdr_len by 4. The only array sized from hdr_length, Unknown[hdr_length-4] at line 87, is in the else branch and stands in for a whole non-IPv4 network header, not for IP options.
Layer_3.ip_hdr_len.completeness_rationale: the field is 4 bits wide, so 0..15 is the entire domain, and 0..4 are exactly the values the decoder refuses. A value above 15 is not encodable.
Layer_3.ip_hdr_len.notes: ip_hdr_len is the multiplier behind four separate length expressions: line 93 ip_hdr_length = VER_HDR*4, line 114 packet[total_length-ip_hdr_length], line 162 AppDataLen = total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 - tcp_hdr_len*4, and line 177's padding. Because the IPv4 branch writes a fixed 20 octets, the only value that keeps all four consistent with the bytes on disk is 5, so this entry pins 5 and the rewrite should not offer the field for diversity. Emitting 6..15 would not merely waste effort - it would shift the transport header by 4 octets per extra word and make print-ip.c read the first bytes of the TCP or UDP header as IP options, which under -v reports "[bad opt]" and under -nr mis-demuxes the ports. IP options are therefore out of reach for this template in either direction: they cannot be emitted, and a header length that claims them corrupts the record.

Layer_3.DiffServField.tier_rationale: No decoder validates it: print-ip.c reads ip->ip_tos only inside the ndo_vflag branch to print "tos 0x%x" and to decode DSCP/ECN names, so under 'tcpdump -nr' the byte is never even examined, and any of the 256 values yields an identically-processed file.
Layer_3.DiffServField.description: The Differentiated Services / Type of Service octet: a 6-bit DSCP, a 2-bit Explicit Congestion Notification field in the original definition, or the older 3-bit precedence plus TOS bits.
Layer_3.DiffServField.notes: Read as a whole byte by the .bt, which is correct: RFC 2474 redefined the octet as 6-bit DSCP + 2-bit CU, and RFC 3168 later fixed the low two bits as ECN. tcpdump decodes both interpretations under -v via bittok2str(ip_tos_values,...). Leave all 256 values free; the ECN sub-field (bits 0-1) is worth varying as a diversity axis because it is the only part with a defined meaning a future verbose-mode checker would look at.

Layer_3.total_length.tier_rationale: print-ip.c:362-365 is a hard gate: 'if (len < hlen) { ND_PRINT("[total length %u < header length %u]", len, hlen); goto invalid; }', and the invalid label calls nd_print_invalid() and returns, so a total_length below ip_hdr_len*4 stops the datagram before any transport-layer dissection. It is also the multiplicand behind every payload length the template computes.
Layer_3.total_length.description: Total length of the IPv4 datagram in octets, header and payload included; must equal the number of datagram bytes actually present in the record.
Layer_3.total_length.algorithm: total_length = ip_hdr_len*4 + L4_header_length + application_data_length, where L4_header_length is 8 for UDP (Layer_4.udp_hdr_len must equal it), tcp_hdr_len*4 for TCP, and 0 for the 'unknown Layer 4' branch. The minimum legal value is ip_hdr_len*4 (20 for a 5-word header) and the maximum is 65535 (RFC 791 section 3.1), but the practical maximum is the bytes the record can hold: total_length <= incl_len - len_before_l3, where len_before_l3 is 14 for LINKTYPE_ETHERNET, 18 when a Dot1q tag is present, and 0 for LINKTYPE_RAW. Equivalently, incl_len = len_before_l3 + total_length + padding_length, which is exactly the identity line 176 inverts to size the padding array.
Layer_3.total_length.covers: The entire IPv4 datagram: the header octets from version/ip_hdr_len through DST_IP (or the Unknown[] option blob), the transport header and the application data. It does not cover the Ethernet or 802.1Q link header and it does not cover the trailing Layer 2 Padding.
Layer_3.total_length.notes: Three distinct decoder outcomes, all worth emitting: (1) total_length < ip_hdr_len*4 -> "[total length N < header length M] (invalid)", nothing below IP is dissected; (2) total_length > the bytes actually captured -> print-ip.c:347-351 prints "[total length %u > length %u]" followed by " (invalid)" but does NOT goto invalid; it continues with the payload bounded by ND_MIN(length - hlen, len) at line 494, so the L4 header may be cut off; (3) total_length == 0 with L4proto TCP or UDP -> print-ip.c:352-360 treats it as a checksum/TSO offload artefact, sets presumed_offload and substitutes len = length, a branch no other value reaches. Case (2) is a soft warning rather than a refusal, which is why the algorithm above is stated as an identity to satisfy rather than a bound to respect.

Layer_3.Identification.tier_rationale: No decoder validates it and under 'tcpdump -nr' it is not even printed: print-ip.c reads ip->ip_id only inside the ndo_vflag branch at line 415 to emit "id %u", so all 65536 values yield an identically-processed file.
Layer_3.Identification.description: 16-bit datagram identifier assigned by the sender to aid in reassembling fragments; RFC 791 imposes no value constraint on it.
Layer_3.Identification.notes: Free 16-bit axis. Repeating one Identification across the fragments of a notional datagram would be more realistic, but the decoder does not attempt reassembly, so it is cosmetic.

Layer_3.Flags.tier_rationale: The 13-bit fragment-offset sub-field gates all transport-layer dissection: print-ip.c:469 'if ((off & IP_OFFMASK) == 0)' is the only path that calls ip_demux_print(); the else branch at lines 496-517 just prints "%s > %s:" plus "ip-proto-%u" (that form because -n is set, so ndo_nflag makes the netdb_protoname lookup at line 513 unreachable) and returns. A nonzero fragment offset therefore reaches no TCP, UDP, ICMP or any other upper-layer printer for that packet.
Layer_3.Flags.description: The combined 3-bit flags and 13-bit fragment-offset field of RFC 791 section 3.1; the fragment offset must be zero for the datagram to be treated as the first, or only, fragment.
Layer_3.Flags.valid_bits: 0x8000 = bit 0, reserved, MUST be zero per RFC 791 (no decoder rejects a set bit, but it is not a legal datagram). 0x4000 = IP_DF, don't fragment; free, printed as "DF" by bittok2str(ip_frag_values,...) at print-ip.c:418 under -v. 0x2000 = IP_MF, more fragments; free, and additionally passed as the 'fragmented' argument to ip_demux_print() at print-ip.c:494, where it only suppresses the checksum computation in tcp_print (print-tcp.c:421) and udp_print (print-udp.c:504) - both already gated on ndo_vflag. 0x1FFF = IP_OFFMASK, the fragment offset in 8-octet units; MUST be 0 for the L4 printers to be reached.
value_names: 0x0000 = no flags, offset 0 - the unfragmented datagram; the only value that yields full transport-layer dissection with no warning text
0x2000 = IP_MF only, offset 0 - first fragment of a fragmented datagram; still reaches ip_demux_print and sets 'fragmented', so the verbose-only checksum verification is skipped
0x4000 = IP_DF only, offset 0 - unfragmented with don't-fragment set; reaches ip_demux_print identically to 0x0000
0x6000 = IP_DF|IP_MF, offset 0 - contradictory but parsed; reaches ip_demux_print with 'fragmented' set
Layer_3.Flags.completeness_rationale: the field is 16 bits wide and all 65536 values are legal IPv4, so no list of four entries can honestly claim to be every legal value. valid_values holds the four combinations of the two defined flag bits (DF, MF) with the fragment offset zero, which are the only values that let tcpdump reach ip_demux_print. The remaining 65532 either carry a nonzero fragment offset or set the reserved bit; they are legal IP that tcpdump deliberately refuses to dissect below the IP layer, so they are excluded from valid_values because they cost the whole Layer_4 subtree, and are offered instead as a separate depth axis in diversity_axes.
Layer_3.Flags.notes: Recorded close call: a nonzero fragment offset is not an invalid datagram, so under a strict 'decoder refuses the file' reading this would be Tier B. It is placed in Tier A because the prompt lists 'offsets that gate further parsing' there and because losing ip_demux_print removes every upper-layer printer from the output. The .bt names the field Flags and treats it as one opaque uint16, so the nibble split exists only in this specification.

Layer_3.TTL.tier_rationale: Never a gate: TTL is passed to ip_demux_print as ttl_hl and consumed by only three printers - vrrp_print (print-vrrp.c:118), carp_print (print-carp.c:61) and esp_print - and in each case a value other than 255 merely adds a warning such as ", (ttl %u)" or "[ttl=%u!] " while dissection continues. Under 'tcpdump -nr' with L4proto TCP or UDP it is not read at all.
Layer_3.TTL.description: Time to live in hops; RFC 791 says a datagram must be discarded when it reaches 0, but no savefile decoder enforces that and tcpdump prints any value 0..255.
Layer_3.TTL.notes: Leave free. If the generator emits L4proto = 112 (VRRP) or 50 (ESP), prefer 255 for that record so the output stays clean, since both printers special-case 255; see the TTL dependency entry.

Layer_3.HdrChecksum.tier_rationale: Tier A by the specification's own rule that every CRC/checksum field is a Tier A calculated_value, and because a real IP stack does discard a datagram with a bad header checksum. Recorded honestly: it is coverage-neutral for THIS checker. tcpdump's only verification is print-ip.c:440-449, which is inside the ndo_vflag branch, so 'tcpdump -nr' never computes it; and even when computed, a mismatch only appends ", bad cksum %x (->%x)!" and dissection continues - there is no goto invalid.
Layer_3.HdrChecksum.description: 16-bit one's-complement checksum over the IPv4 header only, RFC 791 section 3.1; covers no payload.
Layer_3.HdrChecksum.algorithm: Standard RFC 1071 internet checksum over the ip_hdr_len*4 header octets with the two HdrChecksum octets themselves treated as zero: sum every 16-bit big-endian word, folding each carry back into the low 16 bits, then store the one's complement of the result. This is exactly libpcap/tcpdump's in_cksum(vec, 1) with vec[0].ptr = ip and vec[0].len = hlen (print-ip.c:441-444). A receiver verifies by running the same sum WITH the checksum field included and requiring a result of zero.
Layer_3.HdrChecksum.covers: The ip_hdr_len*4 octets of the IPv4 header, from version/ip_hdr_len through DST_IP (or through the end of the Unknown[] option blob). It does not cover the transport header, the transport payload, any link-layer header or the trailing padding.
Layer_3.HdrChecksum.notes: Compute it with the field zeroed, then write it; that is what includes_self = true means here and it is what makes the verify-by-summing-to-zero property hold. Because the header length is variable, the covered region must be recomputed whenever ip_hdr_len changes. Deprecated by RFC 6864 for IPv4 datagrams that do not fragment, but still expected by tcpdump under -v.

Layer_3.Unknown.description: A stand-in for an entire non-IPv4 network header: hdr_length-4 octets occupying everything after the four octets the struct has already consumed (the version/ip_hdr_len bitfield octet, DiffServField and total_length). Layer_3.Unknown.covers: Network-header octets 4 through ip_hdr_len*4 - 1 of a header whose type is not IPv4. It covers no octet of any IPv4 header: the IPv4 branch at lines 75-84 declares Identification, Flags, TTL, L4proto, HdrChecksum, SRC_IP and DST_IP explicitly and emits no array at all.
Layer_3.Unknown.notes: This is NOT the IP options field, despite the earlier reading of this template that said so. RFC 791 options would sit after DST_IP inside the IPv4 branch, and this template has no array there - lines 75-84 emit a fixed 20-octet IPv4 header and nothing more.
