Layer_4.udp_hdr_len.tier_rationale: Two hard gates. In the decoder, print-udp.c:380-381 is ND_ICHECKMSG_ZU("undersized-udplength", ulen, <, sizeof(struct udphdr)), which prints " [undersized-udplength %u < 8]" and 'goto invalid' (the label at line 697 calls nd_print_invalid and returns), so any value below 8 kills the datagram before the port demux. In the template, line 170 computes 'local uint AppDataLen = L4.udp_hdr_len-8' in UNSIGNED arithmetic, so a value below 8 wraps to about 4e9, line 171's 'if (AppDataLen > 0)' passes, and line 173 tries to read four gigabytes.
Layer_4.udp_hdr_len.description: Despite the .bt's <name="Datagram Length"> label this is the UDP length field of RFC 768: the total octet count of the UDP header plus its data, minimum 8.
Layer_4.udp_hdr_len.algorithm: udp_hdr_len = 8 + AppDataLen, where AppDataLen is the length line 170 recovers from it; equivalently udp_hdr_len = total_length - ip_hdr_len*4. The two must agree or line 176's padding identity (incl_len = len_before_l3 + total_length + padding) no longer describes the bytes actually written and the next PCAPRECORD starts at the wrong offset. Minimum 8, maximum 65535, and never more than the bytes present after the IP header.
Layer_4.udp_hdr_len.covers: The 8 octets of the UDP header itself (SrcPort, DstPort, udp_hdr_len, ChkSum) plus every application-data octet that follows, i.e. the whole UDP datagram. It does not cover the IP header, any link-layer header, or the trailing padding.
Layer_4.udp_hdr_len.notes: The field name in the .bt is misleading - it is the datagram length, not a header length, and the 8 in line 170 is the fixed UDP header size rather than a variable. Two further decoder branches are worth hitting: print-udp.c:377-378 substitutes ulen = length when ulen == 0 and length > 65535 (the RFC 2675 IPv6 jumbo case, unreachable here because version is pinned to 4), and print-udp.c:384-385 'if (ulen < length) length = ulen;' bounds the payload by the smaller of the two, so UNDER-declaring udp_hdr_len silently hides trailing application data from the port demux while OVER-declaring it is bounded by the captured bytes and produces no error.

Layer_4.ChkSum.tier_rationale: Tier A by the specification's own rule that every CRC/checksum field is a Tier A calculated_value, and because a real UDP receiver discards a datagram with a bad checksum (RFC 768 also forbids the value 0 over IPv4). Recorded honestly: it is coverage-neutral for THIS checker. tcpdump's only verification is print-udp.c:504, guarded by 'if (ndo->ndo_vflag && !ndo->ndo_Kflag && !fragmented)', so 'tcpdump -nr' never computes it; and even when computed a mismatch only prints "[bad udp cksum 0x%04x -> 0x%04x!] " at lines 519 and 531 and dissection continues.
Layer_4.ChkSum.description: 16-bit one's-complement checksum over a 12-byte IPv4 pseudo-header plus the entire UDP datagram, RFC 768.
Layer_4.ChkSum.algorithm: RFC 1071 internet checksum over a two-element vector, exactly what nextproto4_cksum() builds at print-ip.c:135-162. vec[0] is the 12-octet IPv4 pseudo-header: SRC_IP (4 octets), DST_IP (4 octets), one zero octet, the L4proto octet, and the UDP length as a big-endian uint16 (2 octets). vec[1] is the udp_hdr_len octets of the UDP header and data with these two ChkSum octets treated as zero. Fold every carry into the low 16 bits, then store the one's complement. Equivalent single-pass form: sum the pseudo-header words, then every 16-bit word of the datagram with the checksum field zeroed, pad with one zero octet if the datagram length is odd, fold, complement.
Layer_4.ChkSum.covers: The 12-octet IPv4 pseudo-header (Layer_3.SRC_IP, Layer_3.DST_IP, a zero octet, Layer_3.L4proto, Layer_4.udp_hdr_len) plus the udp_hdr_len octets of the UDP datagram: SrcPort, DstPort, udp_hdr_len, the zeroed ChkSum itself, and all application data. It covers no link-layer header, no IP header field other than those listed, and no trailing padding.
Layer_4.ChkSum.notes: Compute with the field zeroed, then write it - that is what includes_self = true means and what makes verify-by-summing-to-zero work. Because the pseudo-header carries both IP addresses and the UDP length, the value must be recomputed whenever any of them changes. The value 0 means 'no checksum' in UDP: legal over IPv6, deprecated over IPv4, and reported by tcpdump as "[no cksum]" rather than validated, so it is a legitimate third outcome to emit occasionally.

Layer_4.SEQ.tier_rationale: No decoder validates a sequence number and every value is legal: print-tcp.c:257 reads th_seq unconditionally and prints it, and the only branch keyed on it is the relative-sequence bookkeeping at line 275, which is reached for any value. Under 'tcpdump -nr' without -S the printed number is merely relative to the first one seen for the conversation.
Layer_4.SEQ.description: 32-bit TCP sequence number, RFC 9293 section 3.1; the octet offset of this segment's first data byte within the connection's sequence space.
Layer_4.SEQ.notes: Free in all 32 bits, including 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF. It does carry real decoder behaviour worth exploiting as a diversity axis rather than constraining: print-tcp.c:275 'if (!ndo->ndo_Sflag && (flags & TH_ACK))' looks up or records the initial sequence number for the (src, dst, sport, dport) conversation in tcp_seq_hash and subtracts it, so the FIRST segment of a conversation with ACK set establishes the base and later segments print relative offsets. Reusing one 4-tuple across records with varying SEQ therefore exercises the hash-hit path; a fresh 4-tuple exercises the hash-miss path.

Layer_4.ACK.tier_rationale: No decoder validates an acknowledgement number: print-tcp.c:258 reads th_ack unconditionally and it is printed only when the ACK flag is set (line 462) or under -v (line 465), so every value is accepted and processing is identical.
Layer_4.ACK.description: 32-bit TCP acknowledgement number, RFC 9293 section 3.1; meaningful only when the ACK control bit is set.
Layer_4.ACK.notes: Free in all 32 bits. Its printed form is governed by the ACK bit inside Layer_4.Crap[0] rather than by this field: print-tcp.c:462 prints 'ack %u' only when flags & TH_ACK, and line 465 adds the verbose variant. Pairing a nonzero ACK with the ACK flag clear is legal and simply prints nothing.

Layer_4.tcp_hdr_len.tier_rationale: Two hard gates. In the decoder, print-tcp.c:249-255 computes hlen = TH_OFF(tp) * 4 and refuses the segment when it is short: ND_PRINT(" tcp %u [bad hdr length %u - too short, < %zu]", ...) followed by 'goto invalid'; print-tcp.c:415-418 then refuses it when it is too long for the captured bytes, " [bad hdr length %u - too long, > %u]", also 'goto invalid'. In the template, line 110 sizes 'BYTE Crap[tcp_hdr_len*4-13]', which goes negative below 4.
Layer_4.tcp_hdr_len.description: The 4-bit TCP data offset: the header length in 32-bit words. Must be 5..15, and 5..(available bytes / 4) in practice, and it decides whether the Crap array holds only the fixed header tail or an options TLV stream as well.
Layer_4.tcp_hdr_len.field_type: uchar (4-bit bitfield, high nibble of byte 12)
Layer_4.tcp_hdr_len.valid_bits: All four bits are the value; there is no reserved sub-field within the nibble. Under the BigEndian() in force from line 141 this first-declared bitfield occupies the HIGH nibble of the octet, matching tcpdump's TH_OFF(th) = (GET_U_1(th_offx2) & 0xf0) >> 4 at tcp.h:52. The low nibble of the same octet is Layer_4.Reserved.
value_names: 5 = 20-octet header with no options; Crap is then exactly 7 octets (flags, window, checksum, urgent pointer) and print-tcp.c:478 'if (hlen > sizeof(*tp))' is false, so the option walk is skipped entirely
6..15 = 24..60-octet header; Crap is 7 + (tcp_hdr_len-5)*4 octets, of which the last (tcp_hdr_len-5)*4 must be a well-formed TCP options TLV stream, and print-tcp.c:478 enters tcp_opt_print
Layer_4.tcp_hdr_len.completeness_rationale: the field is 4 bits, so 0..15 is the whole domain; 0..4 are exactly the values print-tcp.c:251 refuses, and 5 is the sizeof(struct tcphdr)/4 minimum. Values above 15 are not encodable.
Layer_4.tcp_hdr_len.notes: This is the second multiplicative length in the record and it feeds three expressions: line 110's Crap array, line 162's AppDataLen = total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 - tcp_hdr_len*4, and tcpdump's own payload bound. Preferred values cover the no-options branch (5), the smallest options branch with one 4-octet option such as MSS (6), and an 8-word header big enough for the standard SYN cookie set MSS+SACK-permitted+timestamp+NOP+NOP+WSCALE (8). print-tcp.c:415 means a value that is legal in itself still fails if the record does not actually contain that many bytes, so tcp_hdr_len*4 must never exceed total_length - ip_hdr_len*4.

Layer_4.Reserved.tier_rationale: The .bt calls this field Reserved and it is not: tcpdump's tcp_get_flags() at tcp.h:53-54 is '(GET_U_1(th_flags) | ((GET_U_1(th_offx2) & 0x0f) << 8))', so this low nibble carries TCP control-flag bits 8-11. Bit 0 of the nibble is TH_AE (0x100, Accurate ECN, RFC 9330 / draft-ietf-tcpm-accurate-ecn), which print-tcp.c:114 prints as "e" in the Flags [...] string; bits 1-3 are genuinely reserved. One value in sixteen therefore changes the printed output, which is a finite enumerable behaviour difference rather than a refusal.
Layer_4.Reserved.description: Low nibble of TCP header byte 12: control-flag bits 8-11. Bit 8 (nibble value 1) is Accurate ECN; bits 9-11 are reserved and must be zero in a conforming segment.
Layer_4.Reserved.field_type: uchar (4-bit bitfield, low nibble of byte 12)
Layer_4.Reserved.valid_bits: 0x1 within the nibble = flag bit 8 = TH_AE, Accurate ECN; tcpdump prints it and no decoder rejects it. 0x2, 0x4, 0x8 within the nibble = flag bits 9, 10, 11; reserved by RFC 9293 section 3.1, not validated by libpcap or tcpdump, but they make the segment non-conforming. Under BigEndian() from line 141 this second-declared bitfield occupies the LOW nibble, complementary to tcp_hdr_len's high nibble.
value_names: 0 = all four bits clear; the Flags [...] string shows only the eight bits from Layer_4.Crap[0]
1 = TH_AE set; print-tcp.c:271 emits bittok2str_nosep(tcp_flag_values, "none", flags) with TH_AE mapped to "e", so a segment carrying SYN|ACK|AE prints as "Flags [S.e]"

2..15 = flag bits 9, 10 and 11 set in any combination, with or without TH_AE. Reserved by RFC 9293 section 3.1 and non-conforming on the wire, but neither libpcap nor tcpdump validates them: tcp_get_flags() at tcp.h:53-54 folds the whole nibble into bits 8-11 of the flags word and bittok2str_nosep simply omits the bits it has no name for, so the printed output is identical to the same value with those bits clear. They are recorded here because they are legal as far as the decoder is concerned and each is a distinct 16-way choice on a field that costs nothing; 1..15 with TH_AE set are the four values that also print "e".
Layer_4.Reserved.completeness_rationale: the field is a 4-bit nibble, so 0..15 is the entire domain and all sixteen values are listed. Only bit 0 (TH_AE, Accurate ECN, RFC 9330) has a defined meaning and only it changes tcpdump's output; bits 1-3 are reserved by RFC 9293 section 3.1, make the segment non-conforming, and are parsed and printed identically to their clear state. They are legal-but-shallower values and are recorded rather than dropped, with the two productive ones named in preferred_value.
Layer_4.Reserved.notes: Recorded as a naming trap in the template: a rewriter reading 'Reserved:4' would reasonably zero it, silently deleting the only route to tcpdump's Accurate-ECN branch. The same nibble is where the obsolete NS (Nonce Sum, RFC 3540) bit lived, which is why TH_AE reuses bit 8 rather than being appended.

Layer_4.Crap.tier_rationale: It is the whole remainder of the TCP header, and its trailing options area is a hard gate: print-tcp.c:493-498 rejects any option whose length byte is < 2 or > the remaining header length, and line 504 defines the per-kind check ('#define LENCHECK(l) { if ((l) > hlen) goto bad; }') applied by every case in lines 511-735. The 'bad' label at line 876 prints "[bad opt]" and returns, so a malformed option stream kills not just the option decode but everything after it - the ", length %u" print at line 747, the bounds check at 758, the RST branch at 764 and the entire application-layer port demux at lines 788-872.
Layer_4.Crap.description: The TCP header tail plus the options area: tcp_hdr_len*4 - 13 octets starting at header byte 13, because lines 104-109 already consumed bytes 0-12. The .bt's dismissive name hides the control flags, the window size, the checksum, the urgent pointer and the whole options TLV stream.
Layer_4.Crap.codec: TCP fixed header tail (7 octets) followed by the RFC 793 / RFC 6691 option TLV stream: kind(1) [length(1) value(length-2)], where kinds 0 (EOL) and 1 (NOP) are zero-length and carry no length octet (print-tcp.c:100 '#define ZEROLENOPT(o) ((o) == TCPOPT_EOL || (o) == TCPOPT_NOP)').
Layer_4.Crap.must_produce: Octet layout of Crap, indexed from 0: Crap[0] = control flags (FIN 0x01, SYN 0x02, RST 0x04, PSH 0x08, ACK 0x10, URG 0x20, ECE 0x40, CWR 0x80); Crap[1..2] = window size, big-endian; Crap[3..4] = checksum, big-endian; Crap[5..6] = urgent pointer, big-endian; Crap[7..] = the options area, exactly (tcp_hdr_len - 5) * 4 octets when tcp_hdr_len > 5. The options area must be a sequence of well-formed TLVs padded to a 4-octet multiple with kind 0 (EOL) or kind 1 (NOP), each TLV's length byte >= 2, <= the octets remaining in the area, and >= 2 + the kind-specific datalen print-tcp.c checks. Legal kinds and required total lengths: 0 EOL (1 octet, terminates the loop), 1 NOP (1), 2 MSS (4: kind len 02 02 mss-hi mss-lo), 3 window scale (3), 4 SACK-permitted (2), 5 SACK (2 + 8n; datalen % 8 != 0 makes print-tcp.c:524 print " invalid sack"), 6 ECHO (6), 7 ECHOREPLY (6), 8 timestamps (10: kind len 0A TSval(4) TSecr(4)), 11 CC (6), 12 CCNEW (6), 13 CCECHO (6), 19 MD5 signature (18), 20 SCPS (4), 28 user timeout (4), 29 TCP-AO (>= 4), 30 MPTCP (>= 4), 34 TCP Fast Open (6 or 10, i.e. a 4- or 8-octet cookie), 254 experimental (>= 4, with the leading 2-octet magic 0xF989 selecting the TFO sub-parser). Any other kind prints as 'unknown-%u' from tok2str at line 507 and is still accepted provided its length byte is consistent.
Layer_4.Crap.decoder_gate: A length byte below 2 or above the remaining header length, or a kind whose datalen overruns it, sends print-tcp.c to 'bad' at line 876: it prints "[bad opt]", closes any open bracket and returns. Nothing downstream runs - no ", length N", no port demux, no ftp_print/http_print/domain_print/bgp_print. A length byte of 2 for a kind that needs more (MSS, timestamps) also trips LENCHECK. Random bytes therefore lose the entire TCP application layer for that record.
Layer_4.Crap.generation_strategy: Set tcp_hdr_len = 5 for most records and emit Crap as exactly 7 octets: the flags byte, window(2), checksum(2), urgent(2). For records that should exercise the option parser, set tcp_hdr_len = 6, 7, 8 or 9 and fill Crap[7..] with whole TLVs, padding to the 4-octet multiple with NOP (0x01). A SYN record at tcp_hdr_len 9 wants 02 04 05 B4 (MSS 1460) then 04 02 (SACK-permitted) then 08 0A <TSval4> <TSecr4> then 01 (NOP). A plain data record at tcp_hdr_len 7 wants just 08 0A <TSval4> <TSecr4> then 01 01 (two NOPs). Never split a TLV across the end of the options area, never emit a length byte of 0 or 1 for a kind other than 0 and 1, and keep the total options octet count exactly (tcp_hdr_len - 5) * 4.
Layer_4.Crap.algorithm: length = tcp_hdr_len*4 - 13, so 7 octets for a 5-word header and 7 + (tcp_hdr_len-5)*4 for a longer one. A negative length, i.e. tcp_hdr_len < 4, makes line 110 ill-formed and the .bt parse fails outright.
Layer_4.Crap.covers: TCP header octets 13 through tcp_hdr_len*4 - 1: the control flags, the window size, the checksum, the urgent pointer and the options area. It covers no application data, which line 162 sizes separately.
Layer_4.Crap.notes: The highest-value field in this template precisely because its name discourages anyone from constraining it. Crap[0] is the only route to the flag-gated branches at print-tcp.c:454 (SYN, FIN or RST force the seq/ack/window block to print even with zero payload length), 462 (ACK enables the relative-sequence hash lookup at line 275 and prints 'ack') and 470 (URG prints 'urg'); Crap[1..2] is pure diversity; Crap[3..4] is a checksum that 'tcpdump -nr' never verifies. content_is_free is false because for tcp_hdr_len > 5 the option octets ARE the structure being validated - there is no unconstrained interior to free up. Two kinds buy real depth cheaply: timestamps (kind 8) is the commonest option on the wire and its TSval/TSecr words are free content inside a fixed 10-octet frame, and SACK (kind 5) with datalen 8n drives the block-list loop at print-tcp.c:524-540.

Layer_4.packet.tier_rationale: Two gates. Its length keeps the record self-describing: line 114 sizes it total_length - ip_hdr_length with ip_hdr_length = VER_HDR*4 from line 93, so a mismatch makes the octets written disagree with incl_len and every following PCAPRECORD begins at the wrong offset, which libpcap rejects in sf-pcap.c:744-753 with "truncated dump file" or in sf-pcap.c:589-609 as an invalid capture length. Its content then decides whether a named protocol printer runs at all: ip_demux_print (print-ip-demux.c:49-230) hands these bytes to icmp_print, igmp_print, gre_print, sctp_print, ospf_print, vrrp_print, bgp-over-pim, eigrp_print, dccp_print, rsvp_print, esp_print, ah_print, ipcomp_print, mobile_print, nhrp_print, egp_print or igrp_print, and each of those fails its own header check on random bytes and prints "[|<proto>]" or "(invalid)" instead of descending.
Layer_4.packet.description: The opaque transport-layer payload used when Layer_3.L4proto is neither 6 (TCP) nor 17 (UDP): every octet of the IP datagram after the IP header, whatever protocol L4proto names.
Layer_4.packet.codec: protocol-selected, chosen by Layer_3.L4proto through tcpdump's ip_demux_print(). The named-printer set reachable with Layer_3.version pinned to 4 is protocol numbers 1 (ICMP), 2 (IGMP), 4 (IP-in-IP), 8 (EGP), 9 (IGRP), 33 (DCCP), 46 (RSVP), 47 (GRE), 50 (ESP), 51 (AH), 54 (NHRP), 55 (MOBILE), 88 (EIGRP), 89 (OSPF), 103 (PIM), 108 (IPComp), 112 (VRRP), 113 (PGM) and 132 (SCTP). Numbers 58 (ICMPv6) and 143 (Ethernet) are IPv6-only: with version 4 they print "[ICMPv6 requires IPv6]" and "[ethernet requires IPv6]" (print-ip-demux.c:59-62, 161-166). Number 77 (ND) prints only " nd %u" and 59 (NONE) only "no next header"; every remaining number reaches the default branch at lines 225-231, which prints the protocol name and the length and never reads a byte.
Layer_4.packet.must_produce: For one of the named-printer protocol numbers, a complete minimum message for that protocol with every internal length, count and magic consistent. For any other number, arbitrary octets - nothing reads them. In all cases the octet count must be exactly total_length - ip_hdr_len*4, and total_length must in turn agree with incl_len and the octets actually present.
Layer_4.packet.decoder_gate: A wrong protocol number is not a rejection at all: the default branch prints the name and length and stops, which is a shallow but perfectly legal outcome. For a named number with random bytes the printer's own header check fires - icmp_print '[|icmp]', sctp_print '[bad chunk length]', ospf_print '[ospf: truncated]', bgp-less PIM/IGMP similar - and the body never runs. The length gate is the harder one: a packet[] shorter than total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 desynchronises the record and libpcap aborts the rest of the file.
Layer_4.packet.generation_strategy:
Prefer protocol numbers 1 (ICMP) and 2 (IGMP) for the cheap wins, 47 (GRE) and 4 (IP-in-IP) for the nested-datagram win, and 132 (SCTP), 89 (OSPF), 88 (EIGRP), 112 (VRRP) and 103 (PIM) for the deep per-message switches. Use the table below. Keep the payload length exactly total_length - ip_hdr_len*4, and remember that GRE and IP-in-IP recursively hand their contents back to ip_print, so a nested 20-octet IPv4 header plus a real transport header there buys a second full dissection for the price of one datagram.

Layer_4.packet recipes for non-TCP, non-UDP values of Layer_3.L4proto, keyed by protocol number (tcpdump ip_demux_print(), print-ip-demux.c:49-230).
1 (icmp_print): type(1) code(1) checksum(2) then a type-specific body. Type 8 (Echo Request) and type 0 (Echo Reply) take identifier(2) sequence(2) then free data - the cheapest way in. Types 3 (Dest Unreachable), 4 (Source Quench), 5 (Redirect) and 11 (Time Exceeded) take a 4-octet unused/pointer field followed by the ORIGINAL IPv4 header plus its first 8 payload octets, and icmp_print then recurses into that embedded datagram, which is the deepest single choice here. Types 13/14 (Timestamp) take originate/receive/transmit timestamps, types 17/18 (Address Mask) take a 4-octet mask, types 9/10 (Router Solicit/Advert) take count(1) addr-entry-size(1) lifetime(2) then entries.
2 (igmp_print): version/type(1)=0x11 (IGMPv2 Membership Query) or 0x22 (IGMPv3) max-response-time(1) checksum(2) group-address(4). IGMPv3 adds record-count(2) and group records, which igmp_print walks.
4 (ip_print (nested IPv4)): A complete second IPv4 header with the same 20-octet layout as Layer_3, version 4 and ip_hdr_len 5, followed by its own transport header. This is IP-in-IP tunnelling and ip_demux_print calls ip_print recursively, so one level of nesting is the highest-value single choice for this protocol number.
8 (egp_print): version(1)=2 type(1)=1 (update) code(1) status(1) hello-interval(2) poll-interval(2) then the neighbour reachability data.
9 (igrp_print): version(1)=1 opcode(1)=1 (update) checksum(1) edition(1) reserved(2) autonomous-system(2) then route entries of 14 octets each (network(3) delay(3) bandwidth(3) reliability/load(3) metric(2)); the entry count is derived from the datagram length.
33 (dccp_print): src-port(2) dst-port(2) data-offset(1) ccval(4 bits)+csv(4 bits) checksum(2) reserved(1) type(4 bits)+x(1 bit) then the sequence numbers. dccp_print switches on the type field, so DCCP-Request (0), DCCP-Data (3) and DCCP-Reset (9) are three distinct paths.
46 (rsvp_print): version(4 bits)=1 flags(4 bits) message-type(1)=1 (Path) or 2 (Resv) checksum(2) then RSVP objects of length(2) class(1) c-type(4 bits)+flags(4 bits) value. rsvp_print switches on both the message type and each object class.
47 (gre_print): flags(2)=0x0000 for the plain form, protocol-type(2)=0x0800 for inner IPv4, then the inner IP datagram. The checksum bit (0x8000) adds checksum(2) and reserved1(2); the key bit (0x2000) adds key(4); the sequence bit (0x1000) adds sequence(4). gre_print recurses into the inner protocol, so the inner datagram is where the depth is.
50 (esp_print): spi(4) sequence-number(4) then the encrypted payload. Without esp_secret keys configured, esp_print prints only 'ESP(spi=0x%08x,seq=0x%x)' and the length, so the two 4-octet fields are all that matter; the payload octets are free. spi 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF are both legal and print.
51 (ah_print): next-header(1) header-length(1) reserved(2) spi(4) sequence-number(4) then the ICV of (header-length + 2) * 4 octets. ah_print validates that the header length is consistent and returns the number of octets consumed, which ip_demux_print then advances past and loops on with 'goto again' - so a correct header-length lets the datagram continue into the encapsulated protocol.
54 (nhrp_print): NHRP header: type(2) length(2) checksum(2) then the mandatory part of source/destination address entries. nhrp_print switches on the type field, with 1 (Resolution Request), 2 (Resolution Reply), 3 (Next Hop Resolution Purge) and 4 (Next Hop Registration) as the deep paths.
55 (mobile_print): type(1)=1 (Home Agent Foreign Agent Registration) flags(1) length(2)=24 then the registration request/reply body of lifetime(2) home-address(4) care-of-address(4) identifier(4) and the authenticator extension.
59 (no next header): ip_demux_print's IPPROTO_NONE case is ND_PRINT("no next header") - a legal, shallow terminal choice whose payload content is never read.
77 (no printer): ip_demux_print's IPPROTO_ND case is ND_PRINT(" nd %u", length) and nothing else - the bytes are never examined, so this protocol number is a shallow but legal choice and its payload content is entirely free.
88 (eigrp_print): version(1)=2 opcode(1)=1 (update) checksum(2)=0 autonomous-system(4) then EIGRP TLVs of type(2) length(2) value. eigrp_print switches on the TLV type, with 0x0001 (Parameter), 0x0002 (Authentication), 0x0102 (Internal Route) and 0x0103 (External Route) as the deep paths.
89 (ospf_print): version(1)=2 type(1)=1 (Hello) or 2 (Database Description) or 4 (LS-Request) packet-length(2) router-id(4) area-id(4) checksum(2) auth-type(2) authentication(8) then the type-specific body. For a Hello that is network-mask(4) hello-interval(2) options(1) priority(1) router-dead-interval(4) designated-router(4) backup-router(4) then neighbour router-ids. packet-length must be correct or ospf_print reports a truncated packet.
103 (pim_print): version/type(1)=0x20 (PIMv2, and the low nibble selects the message: 0 = Hello, 8 = Bootstrap, 9 = Assert) reserved(1) checksum(2) then the body. pim_print switches on the low nibble of the first octet, so 0x20 (Hello), 0x28 (Bootstrap) and 0x29 (Assert) are three distinct paths.
108 (ipcomp_print): next-header(1) flags(1) cpi(2) then the compressed payload. ipcomp_print prints the CPI and, when it recognises it as a well-known CPI (e.g. 2 = deflate), names the compression algorithm.
112 (vrrp_print): version/type(1)=0x21 (VRRPv2 Advertisement) virtual-router-id(1) priority(1) count-ip-addresses(1) authentication-type(1)=0 advertisement-interval(1)=100 then count-ip-addresses 4-octet addresses. count-ip-addresses must equal the number of address octets emitted or the printer reports a truncated packet. Note that print-vrrp.c:118-119 appends ', (ttl %u)' whenever the IP TTL is not 255, so TTL 255 is preferred - it is cosmetic, not a gate, and vrrp_print runs either way.
113 (pgm_print): sport(2) dport(2) pgm-length(2) checksum(2) source-port(2) group(2) then the PGM trailer options. pgm_print switches on the type field in the second octet pair, with SPM (0x04), NAK (0x08) and NCF (0x0A) as the deep paths.
132 (sctp_print): src-port(2) dst-port(2) verification-tag(4) checksum(4) then chunks of chunk-type(1) flags(1) length(2) value. sctp_print switches on the chunk type, with 1 (INIT), 3 (SACK), 5 (SELECTIVE ACK), 10 (ABORT) and 12 (SHUTDOWN) as the deep paths, and length must equal the true chunk size or it reports a bad chunk length.
Every other protocol number reaches only the default branch at print-ip-demux.c:225-231, which prints the protocol name from ipproto_string plus ' %u' (the payload length) and never examines a byte, so their payload content is genuinely free.
Layer_4.packet.algorithm: length = total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 (line 114, with ip_hdr_length from line 93). Must be >= 0, so total_length >= ip_hdr_len*4 - the same inequality print-ip.c:362 enforces on the decoder side. When it is 0 the array contributes no octets and the datagram is header-only.
Layer_4.packet.covers: Every octet of the IP datagram after the ip_hdr_len*4 header octets, i.e. the whole transport header and payload for whatever protocol L4proto names. It covers no link-layer header and no trailing Layer 2 Padding.
Layer_4.packet.notes: content_is_free is true here in the split sense the schema intends: the ENVELOPE is Tier A - the octet count must equal total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 and, for a named protocol number, the message header must be well formed - while the bytes inside that header are unconstrained. For ESP (50) and IPComp (108) that split is nearly total, since without decryption keys the printers read only the leading fixed fields and treat the rest as opaque. For the roughly 200 protocol numbers with no named printer the whole array is free and the only thing that matters is its length. L4proto 6 and 17 never reach this array: lines 95-111 give them the TCP and UDP branches instead, so this entry and PCAPRECORD.AppData are mutually exclusive per record.

PCAPRECORD.ts_sec.tier_rationale: No decoder validates a timestamp value: sf-pcap.c:529/534 copies ts.tv_sec straight through (optionally byte-swapped) into the pcap_pkthdr and tcpdump's ts_print() only formats it, so every one of the 2^32 values yields an identically-dissected packet.
PCAPRECORD.ts_sec.description: Seconds since the Unix epoch for the captured packet, as a fixed 32-bit field. With the classic pcap magic this is a tv_sec of struct timeval.
PCAPRECORD.ts_sec.notes: CRITICAL type trap: bt.h declares 'typedef long time_t', which is 8 octets on this 64-bit host, but the classic pcap record header is four fixed 32-bit fields (pcap_sf_patched_pkthdr at sf-pcap.c:167-172, hdrsize 16). The rewrite MUST serialise ts_sec as exactly 4 octets; honouring the .bt's time_t size would shift ts_usec, incl_len and orig_len by four bytes each and desynchronise every record in the file. This is the single most dangerous line in the template and is called out again in the structure section. Values 0 (the epoch) and 0xFFFFFFFF (2106-02-07, the 32-bit wrap) are both parsed; tcpdump's default -tttt rendering of a post-2038 value is implementation-defined but never an error, so the endpoints are free diversity rather than hazards.

PCAPRECORD.ts_usec.tier_rationale: libpcap does not range-check it: sf-pcap.c:530/535 copies ts.tv_usec through and only rescales it for the nanosecond magic (scale_type SCALE_UP/SCALE_DOWN at lines 538-560), never rejecting a value above 999999; tcpdump's ts_print() merely formats it, so all 2^32 values are accepted.
PCAPRECORD.ts_usec.description: Microsecond (or nanosecond, with NSEC_TCPDUMP_MAGIC) fraction of the capture timestamp.
PCAPRECORD.ts_usec.notes: A value above 999999 is semantically invalid for a microsecond field yet is parsed without complaint, which is exactly the Tier C signature - the decoder does not care, so the generator should not either. It is also the field the SCALE_UP path multiplies by 1000 (sf-pcap.c:550), which overflows a 32-bit tv_usec for large inputs; that is a libpcap quirk to be aware of if the nanosecond magic is ever added, not a constraint on this file.

PCAPRECORD.incl_len.tier_rationale: Three hard gates and one silent truncation, all keyed on this field. sf-pcap.c:589-609 returns -1 with "invalid packet capture length %u, bigger than snaplen of %d" (or "...bigger than maximum of %u") when incl_len exceeds max_snaplen_for_dlt(), which is MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN = 262144 for both DLT_EN10MB and DLT_RAW (pcap-common.c:1674-1690), and returning -1 stops the read for the whole rest of the file. sf-pcap.c:744-753 returns -1 with "truncated dump file; tried to read %u captured bytes, only got %zu" if the file does not actually contain incl_len octets after the 16-octet record header. print-ether.c:156-159 prints only " [|ethernet]" when caplen < ETHER_HDRLEN (14). And sf-pcap.c:611-712 silently truncates to snaplen when incl_len > snaplen, discarding the tail.
PCAPRECORD.incl_len.description: Number of octets of the packet actually stored in the file, i.e. the exact byte count of the frame body that follows this 16-octet record header.

evidence.snippet: uint32 incl_len;       /* number of octets of packet saved in file */

PCAPRECORD.incl_len.algorithm: incl_len = len_before_l3 + total_length + padding_len, where len_before_l3 is the local the template itself maintains: 0 for PCAPHEADER.network == 101 (LINKTYPE_RAW, lines 143-145), 14 for LINKTYPE_ETHERNET without a tag (line 148), and 18 when Layer_2.L3type == 0x8100 adds a Dot1q (line 154). padding_len is the value lines 176-177 derive from incl_len, so in the common no-padding case incl_len = len_before_l3 + total_length exactly. Bounds: 14 <= incl_len <= 262144 for LINKTYPE_ETHERNET (print-ether.c:156 needs >= ETHER_HDRLEN), 20 <= incl_len <= 262144 for LINKTYPE_RAW (ip4_print's ND_ICHECK_ZU(length, <, sizeof(struct ip)) needs >= 20 once len_before_l3 is 0), and the file must physically contain that many octets at this offset.
PCAPRECORD.incl_len.covers: Every octet of the frame body that follows the record header: the Layer_2 Ethernet header (or nothing, for LINKTYPE_RAW), the optional Dot1q tag, the whole Layer_3 datagram, the Layer_4 header, the application data and the trailing Layer 2 Padding. It covers none of the 16 record-header octets and none of the 24-octet file header.
PCAPRECORD.incl_len.notes: This field decides where the NEXT record starts, so an error here is not local: it desynchronises every subsequent record and turns the remainder of the file into noise. It is also what the .bt's line 176 padding test inverts, which means incl_len is an INPUT to the template's layout rather than a derived output - the generator must either choose it first and size the padding to match, or choose the padding and compute it. Note the asymmetry with PCAPHEADER.snaplen: exceeding snaplen only truncates, exceeding 262144 aborts the read.

PCAPRECORD.orig_len.tier_rationale: tcpdump's very first check in the Ethernet printer is a comparison against it: print-ether.c:151-155 'if (length < caplen) { ND_PRINT("[length %u < caplen %u]", length, caplen); nd_print_invalid(ndo); return length; }', where length is h->len (orig_len) and caplen is h->caplen (incl_len). An orig_len below incl_len therefore prints one bracketed message and dissects NOTHING - no addresses, no EtherType, no IP, no TCP. On the LINKTYPE_RAW path print-raw.c:43-46 prints "truncated-ip %u" and returns when h->len < 1, and line 53 passes h->len as the sole length argument to ip_print, so orig_len there also supplies ip4_print's ND_ICHECK_ZU(length, <, sizeof(struct ip)) bound.
PCAPRECORD.orig_len.description: Actual length of the packet as it appeared on the wire, in octets; must be at least incl_len, and equal to it unless the capture was deliberately truncated.

evidence.snippet: uint32 orig_len;       /* actual length of packet */

PCAPRECORD.orig_len.algorithm: orig_len = incl_len for an untruncated capture, which is the value to emit in the overwhelming majority of records. orig_len > incl_len is legal and models a truncated capture; it is safe for LINKTYPE_ETHERNET because print-ether.c:151 rejects only length < caplen, but for LINKTYPE_RAW it must not exceed the bytes present, since print-raw.c:53 hands h->len to ip_print as the authoritative length while ip4_print's ND_TTEST and ND_TCHECK macros are bounded by ndo_snapend, so an inflated orig_len triggers " [|ip]" through nd_trunc_longjmp. orig_len < incl_len must never be emitted.
PCAPRECORD.orig_len.covers: No bytes directly; it is a claimed on-the-wire size for the same frame body incl_len counts, and the decoder uses the difference to decide whether the capture was truncated.
PCAPRECORD.orig_len.notes: Two version-dependent traps. (1) With PCAPHEADER.version_minor in {0,1,2} libpcap sets lengths_swapped = SWAPPED (sf-pcap.c:389-397) and unconditionally exchanges caplen and len after reading them, so the ON-DISK order must be (orig_len, incl_len) for the in-memory pair to come out right; with version_minor == 3 (MAYBE_SWAPPED, sf-pcap.c:569-578) libpcap exchanges them only if the first field read is greater than the second, so emitting incl_len > orig_len on disk silently swaps them and produces exactly the length < caplen condition that kills the frame. version_minor == 4 (NOT_SWAPPED) has no such hazard. (2) This libpcap performs NO caplen <= len sanity check of its own for NOT_SWAPPED files - the rejection comes from tcpdump's printer, not from libpcap - so a bad orig_len is invisible to header-level validation and shows up only as " (invalid)" in the decode.

PCAPRECORD.AppData.tier_rationale: Its LENGTH gates a large block of decoder work and its CONTENT decides which application-layer printer runs. print-tcp.c:749-750 is 'if (length == 0) return;' - a zero-length TCP payload skips the entire port demux at lines 788-872, so ftp_print, ssh_print, http_print, domain_print, bgp_print, smb_tcp_print and a dozen others are never entered. print-udp.c:383-386 applies ND_ICHECKMSG_ZU("undersized-udplength", ulen, <, sizeof(struct udphdr)) and then clamps with 'if (ulen < length) length = ulen;', so a UDP length field of 8 hands the demuxed printer zero bytes. And once a printer IS entered with random bytes it fails its own front gate - domain_print aborts on a malformed header, http_print prints nothing without a recognisable request or status line, ssh_print nothing without the 'SSH-' prefix, bgp_print nothing without the 16-octet 0xFF marker - so the octets inside must be a real message for the depth to materialise.
PCAPRECORD.AppData.description: The application-layer message carried by a TCP segment or UDP datagram: AppDataLen octets of protocol payload, emitted at line 165 for TCP and line 173 for UDP. Declared as an opaque BYTE array in both places, at the same struct offset, under the same name.
PCAPRECORD.AppData.codec: port-selected application protocol rather than a single codec. On the UDP side tcpdump's udp_print demuxes 68 ports to named printers (domain_print for DNS and mDNS, bootp_print for DHCP, ntp_print, snmp_print's BER/ASN.1 walker, rip_print, isakmp_print, vxlan_print and geneve_print which recurse into a nested Ethernet frame, radius_print, sip_print, dhcp6_print, l2tp_print, bfd_print, sflow_print, babel_print and others). On the TCP side tcp_print demuxes 22 ports to ftp_print, ssh_print, telnet_print, smtp_print, whois_print, domain_print, http_print, netbios_ssn_print, bgp_print, rpki_rtr_print, smb_tcp_print, rtsp_print, msdp_print, ldp_print, pptp_print, nfs_print, resp_print, openflow_print and beep_print. For every other port the payload is unstructured and free.
PCAPRECORD.AppData.must_produce: For a demuxed port, a complete minimum message for that protocol, including every internal length, count and magic that the protocol's own printer checks. For any other port, arbitrary octets. In both cases the octet count must equal what the enclosing length field claims: for TCP, AppDataLen = total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 - tcp_hdr_len*4 (line 162); for UDP, AppDataLen = udp_hdr_len - 8 (line 170).
PCAPRECORD.AppData.decoder_gate: Zero length: print-tcp.c:749 returns before the demux, so the whole TCP application layer is skipped; print-udp.c:385 clamps length to ulen - 8, so the UDP demux printers receive zero octets and each bails at its own header check. Random bytes with a non-zero length: the correct printer is still selected by port, but it fails its first structural test and prints one bracketed complaint - domain_print '[|domain]', http_print nothing at all, ssh_print nothing, bgp_print '[BGP: Message length %u is less than the minimum header length %u]', snmp_print '[snmp: truncated]', openflow_print '[openflow] (invalid)'. The named printer's body is then never executed, which is exactly the coverage this field buys.
PCAPRECORD.AppData.generation_strategy:
Emit AppDataLen > 0 whenever a demuxed port is chosen, and build the payload from the table below. For non-demuxed ports fill AppDataLen octets freely - zero-fill is acceptable because no printer reads them. Never let AppDataLen exceed what the enclosing length fields claim, and never let the claimed lengths exceed the octets actually written, because both break the record alignment described under PCAPRECORD.incl_len.

UDP payload recipes, keyed by the UDP port that must appear in Layer_4.DstPort or Layer_4.SrcPort (tcpdump's IS_SRC_OR_DST_PORT tests both ends). Each entry is '<port> (<printer>): <octets>'.
53 (domain_print (DNS)): 12-octet DNS header then one question: id(2, free) flags(2)=0x0100 (standard query, RD) qdcount(2)=1 ancount(2)=0 nscount(2)=0 arcount(2)=0; QNAME as label-length prefixed octets 03 'w' 'w' 'w' 07 'e' 'x' 'a' 'm' 'p' 'l' 'e' 03 'c' 'o' 'm' 00 (17 octets); qtype(2)=0x0001 (A) qclass(2)=0x0001 (IN). 33 octets total. flags 0x8180 (response, RD+RA) with ancount=1 and a 4-octet A-record answer takes the answer-parsing half of domain_print instead.
67 (bootp_print (DHCP/BOOTP server)): 236-octet BOOTP header: op(1)=2 (BOOTREPLY) htype(1)=1 hlen(1)=6 hops(1)=0 xid(4) secs(2)=0 flags(2)=0x8000 ciaddr(4)=0 yiaddr(4)=e.g. 192.168.1.100 siaddr(4)=0 giaddr(4)=0 chaddr(16, first 6 = a MAC) sname(64 NUL) file(128 NUL); then the RFC 2131 magic cookie 63 82 53 63; then options as type(1) length(1) value: 53 01 02 (DHCPOFFER), 54 04 c0a80101 (server id), 51 04 00007080 (lease time), 255 (end). bootp_print walks the whole option list.
68 (bootp_print (DHCP/BOOTP client)): Same as port 67 but op(1)=1 (BOOTREQUEST), yiaddr(4)=0 and option 53 01 01 (DHCPDISCOVER); add option 55 (parameter request list) 05 01 03 06 0f 2c 2e 2f to exercise bootp_print's request-list branch.
69 (tftp_print): opcode(2)=0x0001 (RRQ), then a NUL-terminated ASCII filename 'file.bin\0', then a NUL-terminated mode 'octet\0'. opcode 3 (DATA) instead takes blknum(2) then data and reaches the other half of tftp_print.
88 (kerberos_print): BER ASN.1 KRB-AS-REQ: 6A <len> 30 <len> A1 03 02 01 05 A2 03 02 01 0A A3 <len> 30 <len> ... with pvno INTEGER 5 and msg-type INTEGER 10. Lengths must be correct DER short-form (< 0x80) or use 81 xx; kerberos_print's ASN.1 walker rejects a wrong length immediately.
123 (ntp_print): Exactly 48 octets: byte0 = (LI<<6)|(VN<<3)|mode, use 0x24 (LI=0, VN=4, mode=4 server); stratum(1)=2 poll(1)=6 precision(1)=0xEC rootdelay(4)=0 rootdisp(4)=0 refid(4)='GPS\0' then four 64-bit NTP timestamps (reference, originate, receive, transmit) with non-zero seconds parts. ntp_print decodes every one of them, so the timestamps are the depth.
137 (netbios_ns_print): 12-octet NBNS header (id(2), flags(2)=0x8500 broadcast response, qdcount(2)=0, ancount(2)=1, nscount(2)=0, arcount(2)=0) then a first-level-encoded NetBIOS name (' ' padded to 16, then each nibble + 'A': CKAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA\0) then type(1)=0x20, class(2)=0x0001, ttl(4), rdlength(2)=6, flags(2), 6 address octets.
138 (netbios_dgm_print): msgtype(1)=0x11 (direct group), flags(1)=0x02, id(2), source IP(4), source port(2), dgm length(2), packet offset(2), then a source NetBIOS name and a destination NetBIOS name, both first-level encoded as for port 137.
161 (snmp_print): BER: 30 <len> 02 01 00 (version INTEGER 0 = SNMPv1) 04 06 'p' 'u' 'b' 'l' 'i' 'c' (community OCTET STRING) A0 <len> 02 04 <request-id> 02 01 00 02 01 00 30 <len> 30 <len> 06 <oid-len> 2B 06 01 02 01 01 01 00 05 00. That is a GetRequest for sysDescr.0 with a NULL value; snmp_print walks the varbind list.
162 (snmp_print (trap)): Same envelope but PDU tag A4 (SNMPv1 Trap) and a trap body of enterprise OID, agent-addr(4), generic-trap(1), specific-trap(1), time-stamp(4), varbind list.
319 (ptp_print (event)): 34 octets: byte0 = (transportSpecific<<4)|messageType = 0x00 (Sync); byte1 = versionPTP = 0x02; messageLength(2) = 0x0022; domainNumber(1) = 0; byte5 = reserved|alternateMaster = 0; correctionField(8) = 0; byte14-15 reserved = 0; sourcePortIdentity(10) = clockIdentity(8) all zero + portNumber(2) = 1; sequenceId(2); controlField(1) = 0; logMessageInterval(1) = 0x7F.
320 (ptp_print (general)): Same 34-octet layout with byte0 messageType = 0x0B (Announce) and controlField = 5, which selects ptp_print's Announce branch (grandmaster identity, steps removed and time-source octets follow the common header).
443 (quic_print (QUIC over HTTPS)): A QUIC Initial packet: the first octet's long-header form bit must be set, e.g. 0xC3 = header-form 1, fixed-bit 1, type 0 (Initial); then version(4) = 0x00000001, dcid-len(1) = 8, dcid(8), scid-len(1) = 8, scid(8), token-len varint = 0, length varint = 4 + payload, packet-number-offset varint, then the payload. quic_print stops early unless the header-protection sample decrypts, so the honest budget here is the header alone: it reaches quic_print and prints the version and connection IDs, which is more than an unrecognised datagram gets.
496 (cisco_autorp_print): version/type(1) = 0x11 (Auto-RP announcement), reserved(1) = 0, holdtime(2), prefix-length(1), group-count(1), then group-count RP-address entries of 4 octets each; the printer indexes on group-count, so keep it equal to the entries emitted.
500 (isakmp_print): 28-octet ISAKMP header: initiator-cookie(8) responder-cookie(8) next-payload(1)=0 version(1)=0x20 (major 2 minor 0) exchange-type(1)=34 (IKE_SA_INIT) flags(1)=0x08 message-id(4)=0 total-length(4)=0x0000001C. total-length must equal 28 or isakmp_print reports a truncated message and stops at the header.
514 (syslog_print): ASCII: '<' decimal-priority '>' then an RFC 3164 timestamp and the message, e.g. the literal bytes '<134>Jan  1 00:00:00 host prog[1]: hello\n'. Priority must parse as an integer; syslog_print derives facility and severity from it.
520 (rip_print): command(1)=2 (response) version(1)=2 unused(2)=0, then one or more 20-octet route entries: address-family(2)=2 (IP) route-tag(1)=0 unused(1)=0 address(4) subnet-mask(4) next-hop(4) metric(4)=1. rip_print iterates entries until the datagram runs out, so the entry count is free.
521 (ripng_print): command(1)=2 version(1)=1 unused(2)=0, then 20-octet entries: address-family(2)=0 route-tag(1)=0 prefix-length(1)=64 IPv6-prefix(16) metric(1)=1; an entry with address-family 0xFFFF is a next-hop entry and takes ripng_print's other branch.
525 (timed_print): type(1)=1 (TSP_SETDATE) version(1)=1 sequence(2) machine-name-length(2) then that many bytes of NUL-terminated host name.
546 (dhcp6_print (server)): msg-type(1)=2 (ADVERTISE) transaction-id(3) then DHCPv6 options as code(2) length(2) value; use option 23 (DNS recursive name server) 00 10 <16-byte IPv6> and option 3 (IA_NA) 00 04 00 0C ... dhcp6_print walks the option list.
547 (dhcp6_print (client)): msg-type(1)=1 (SOLICIT) transaction-id(3), option 1 (OPTION_CLIENTID) 00 01 00 0A 00 03 <DUID octets>, option 6 (OPTION_ORO) 00 06 00 04 00 17 00 18.
646 (ldp_print): version(2)=1 pdu-length(2)=28 ldp-identifier(6) = router-id(4) + label-space(2), then one mandatory TLV of u-bit(2 bits)+type(10 bits) length(2) value; use type 0x0001 (Common Hello Parameters) length 4 hold-time(2)=0x000F target-hello bit 0 reserved 0.
654 (aodv_print): type(1)=1 (RREQ) reserved(1)=0 hop-count(1)=0 rreq-id(4) dest-addr(4) dest-seq(4) orig-addr(4) orig-seq(4). aodv_print switches on the type octet, so 1 (RREQ), 2 (RREP) and 3 (RERR) are three different deep paths.
698 (olsr_print): packet-length(2) packet-sequence-number(2) then one message: msg-type(1)=1 (HELLO) vtime(1) then the message body; olsr_print recurses on packet-length, which must equal the true total.
701 (lmp_print): version(1)=1 flags(1) msg-type(1)=1 (Config) length(2) node-id(4) then LMP TLVs of class(2) length(2) value; lmp_print switches on msg-type.
750 (kerberos_print (kpasswd)): udp-header-length(2)=6 protocol-version(2)=0xff80 then the port-88 BER KRB-ERROR or KRB-PRIV message.
921 (lwres_print): pkt-version(2)=0 pkt-length(4) context(4) getaddrinfo-request: addrtype(2) namelen(2) then that many octets of NUL-terminated host name.
1589 (vqp_print): version(1)=0x01 opcode(1)=0x01 (join) response-code(1)=0x00 data-count(1)=N sequence(4) then N items of type(4) length(2) value.
1645 (radius_print): code(1)=1 (Access-Request) identifier(1) length(2)=20+attrs authenticator(16) then attributes of type(1) length(2) value; use type 1 (User-Name) len 5 'abc' and type 2 (User-Password) len 18.
1646 (radius_print (accounting)): code(1)=4 (Accounting-Request) then as port 1645 with attribute 40 (Acct-Status-Type) len 6 value 1 (Start).
1700 (radius_print (Cisco CoA)): code(1)=43 (CoA-Request) or 44 (CoA-ACK) then the same attribute list.
1701 (l2tp_print): flags(2)=0xC80A (type=control, length present, sequence present, version 2) length(2)=12 tunnel-id(2) session-id(2) Ns(2)=0 Nr(2)=0 then one AVP of mandatory-bit+type(2) length(2) value; type 0 (SCCRQ) takes the deepest path.
1812 (radius_print (new)): Identical to port 1645; 1812 is the current IANA port.
1813 (radius_print (new accounting)): Identical to port 1646.
1985 (hsrp_print): version(4 bits)=0 opcode(4 bits)=0 state(1)=4 (Active) hellotime(1)=3 holdtime(1)=10 priority(1)=100 group(1)=0 reserved(1)=0 authdata(8) NUL-padded virtual-address(4). Exactly 20 octets.
2049 (nfs_print (either end)): 4-octet RPC record mark with the high bit clear and the fragment length, then a SUNRPC call: xid(4) msg-type(4)=0 (CALL) rpc-version(4)=2 program(4)=100003 (NFS) version(4)=3 procedure(4) then two NULL verifiers (flavour 0, length 0). nfsreq_noaddr_print decodes the procedure arguments.
2103 (zephyr_print (server)): 4-octet magic 0x5A 0x48 0x4D 0x53 ('ZHMS') then version(4) numfields(4)=4 then four NUL-terminated field strings.
2104 (zephyr_print (client)): Same as port 2103.
3456 (vat_print): VAT audio header: a leading flags/type octet then the sample data; reached only for dport 3456, and any bytes work once the datagram is at least 4 octets.
3503 (mpls_lsp_ping_print): version(1)=1 msg-type(1)=1 (echo request) reply-mode(1)=2 return-code(1)=0 return-subcode(1)=0 sender-handle(4) sequence(4) timestamp-sent(8) timestamp-received(8) timestamp-reply(8) then TLVs of type(2) length(2) value; include type 1 (Target FEC Stack).
3784 (bfd_print (control)): 24-octet BFD control packet: byte0 = (version<<5)|diag = 0x20 (version 1, diag 0) byte1 = flags (Sta=3 Up, P=0, F=0) multiplier(1)=3 length(1)=24 my-discriminator(4) your-discriminator(4) desired-min-tx(4) required-min-rx(4) required-min-echo-rx(4).
3785 (bfd_print (echo)): Same 24-octet control header; the printer distinguishes echo by port, not by content.
3799 (radius_print (CoA)): code(1)=43 (CoA-Request) then the same attribute list; this is the IANA-assigned port for the same protocol.
4342 (lisp_control_print): type(1)=1 (Map-Register) reserved(1) then the LISP control header and its EID records; the printer switches on the type octet, with 1, 2 (Map-Request), 3 (Map-Reply) and 5 (Map-Notify) as the deep paths.
4500 (isakmp_rfc3948_print (NAT-T)): 4-octet non-ESP marker 00 00 00 00 followed by exactly the port-500 28-octet ISAKMP header. The leading zero word is what selects the NAT-T path.
4567 (wb_print): DVMRP whiteboard audio header: a version/type octet then the sample data; only dport 4567 reaches it.
4784 (bfd_print (multihop)): Same 24-octet BFD control header.
4789 (vxlan_print): 8-octet VXLAN header: byte0 = 0x08 (flags with the I bit set) bytes1-3 reserved 0 VNI(3) byte7 reserved 0; then an inner Ethernet frame of 14 octets (dst MAC, src MAC, ethertype 0x0800) which vxlan_print hands to ether_print, giving the deepest single choice in this table - a complete nested IPv4/TCP packet.
4790 (vxlan_gpe_print): byte0 = 0x0C (flags with I and P set) bytes1-2 reserved 0 byte3 = next-protocol = 3 (Ethernet), then VNI(3), reserved(1), then the inner Ethernet frame as for 4789.
5060 (sip_print): ASCII request or response terminated by a blank line, e.g. 'OPTIONS sip:bob@example.com SIP/2.0\r\nVia: SIP/2.0/UDP h\r\nFrom: <sip:a@b>;tag=1\r\nTo: <sip:c@d>\r\nCall-ID: 1\r\nCSeq: 1 OPTIONS\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n'. sip_print tokenises the headers, so well-formed CRLF and colon syntax is required, not merely ASCII text.
5353 (domain_print (mDNS)): Exactly the port-53 recipe; domain_print is called with is_mdns TRUE, so it additionally inspects the class field's top bit (0x8001 = cache-flush) and the 224.0.0.251 destination. Emit qclass 0x8001 on a response to reach those branches.
5359 (ahcp_print): version(1)=2 then the AHCP message body TLVs of type(1) length(2) value; ahcp_print switches on version and type.
6081 (geneve_print): 8-octet base header: byte0 = (version<<6)|opt-len = 0x00 (version 0, zero option words) byte1 = flags 0x00 protocol-type(2) = 0x6558 (Transparent Ethernet Bridging) VNI(3) byte7 reserved 0; then an inner Ethernet frame of 14 octets, which geneve_print recurses into. Adding option words means byte0's low six bits must equal the option octet count divided by four.
6343 (sflow_print): version(4)=5 agent-address-type(4)=1 (IPv4) agent-address(4) sub-agent-id(4) sequence-number(4) uptime(4)=1000 num-samples(4)=1 then one sample of enterprise(4) format(4)=1 (flow sample) length(4) sequence(4) source-id(4) sampling-rate(4) sample-pool(4) drops(4) input(4) output(4) num-records(4)=0.
6635 (mpls_print): One or more 4-octet MPLS labels: label(20 bits) TC(3 bits) S(1 bit, set on the bottom label) TTL(8 bits); e.g. 00 12 FF 40 for label 18, TC 0, S=1, TTL 64.
6696 (babel_print): magic(2)=0xBACF plen(1)=0 then TLVs of type(1) length(1) value; use type 1 (Router-Hello) length 6 interval-seq(2) interval(2) rxcost(2).
6697 (babel_print (old)): magic(2)=0x4241 then the same TLV stream; the old magic selects babel_print's legacy parser.
6784 (bfd_print (LAG)): Same 24-octet BFD control header.
7500 (isakmp_print (user1)): Exactly the port-500 28-octet ISAKMP header.
7784 (sbfd_print): Seamless BFD: same 24-octet control layout, distinguished by port.

8472 (vxlan_print (Linux)): Identical to port 4789; the Linux kernel VXLAN port uses the same 8-octet header.
8500 (isakmp_print (user2)): Exactly the port-500 28-octet ISAKMP header.
12222 (lwapp_data_print): LWAPP data header: frame-control(2) length(2) wtp-mac(6) radio-mac(6) then the encapsulated 802.11 frame.
12223 (lwapp_control_print): LWAPP control header: frame-control(2) length(2) sequence(1) message-type(1) then message elements of type(2) length(2) value.

30490 (someip_print): message-id(4) length(4)=8+payload request-id(4) protocol-version(1)=0x01 interface-version(1)=0x01 message-type(1)=0x00 (REQUEST) return-code(1)=0x00 then the serialised arguments.

TCP payload recipes, keyed by the TCP port. Every one of these is reached only when the TCP payload length is non-zero - print-tcp.c:749-750 is 'if (length == 0) return;', which skips the whole demux - and only when the RST flag is clear, print-tcp.c:764-770.
21 (ftp_print): A complete CRLF-terminated FTP line: '220 (vsFTPd 3.0.3)\r\n' from the server side or 'USER anonymous\r\n' from the client side. ftp_print prints the line and returns, so one line is enough; a multi-line reply with a leading 3-digit code and '-' continuation reaches its other branch.
22 (ssh_print): A version-exchange line: the ASCII bytes 'SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.9p1\r\n'. ssh_print matches the 'SSH-' prefix and the two dot-separated version numbers; without them it prints nothing. Following it with the 16-octet binary packet header (packet-length(4) padding-length(1) then payload) reaches the packet walk.
23 (telnet_print): IAC option-negotiation bytes: 0xFF 0xFB 0x01 (IAC WILL ECHO) 0xFF 0xFD 0x01 (IAC DO ECHO) then ASCII 'login: '. telnet_print scans the whole run for 0xFF, so each IAC triple is a branch; sub-negotiation 0xFF 0xFA ... 0xFF 0xF0 is another.
25 (smtp_print): A CRLF-terminated SMTP line: '220 mail.example.com ESMTP Postfix\r\n' or 'EHLO client.example.com\r\n'. smtp_print prints the line verbatim; a multi-line reply '250-mail\r\n250 OK\r\n' reaches its continuation handling.
43 (whois_print): ASCII response text with CR or LF terminators, e.g. 'Domain Name: EXAMPLE.COM\r\nRegistrar: Example Registrar\r\n'. whois_print walks the buffer for line ends, so real text beats random bytes.
53 (domain_print (DNS over TCP)): Two-octet big-endian message length then exactly the port-53/UDP 33-octet DNS message. The length prefix must equal the number of octets that follow or domain_print reports a truncated message.
80 (http_print): An ASCII request or status line with CRLF terminators and a blank line: 'GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n' or 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n'. http_print tokenises on the CRLFs and recognises the verbs and the status line, so both spellings are distinct paths.
139 (netbios_ssn_print): 4-octet NBT session header: type(1)=0x00 (session message) flags(1)=0x00 length(2)=the SMB octet count that follows; then an SMB1 header 0xFF 'S' 'M' 'B' or an SMB2 header 0xFE 'S' 'M' 'B' with a 64-octet fixed header. nbt_tcp_print switches on the session type.
179 (bgp_print): 19-octet BGP KEEPALIVE: marker(16) = sixteen 0xFF octets, length(2) = 0x0013, type(1) = 4 (KEEPALIVE). Type 1 (OPEN) instead takes bgp_print's longest path: version(1)=4 hold-time(2) bgp-id(4) opt-param-len(1) then capabilities of code(1) len(1) value. The 16-octet all-0xFF marker is checked first and a wrong marker aborts the message walk.
323 (rpki_rtr_print): protocol-version(1)=1 pdu-type(1)=10 (Cache Response) session-id(2) length(4)=12 then the payload; rpki_rtr_print switches on the PDU type, with 2 (End of Data), 4 (IPv4 Prefix) and 10 as the deepest.
445 (smb_tcp_print): 4-octet NetBIOS session header of type 0x00 and the SMB length, then 0xFF 'S' 'M' 'B' plus the 28-octet SMB1 fixed header, or 0xFE 'S' 'M' 'B' plus the 64-octet SMB2 fixed header with a valid command field. smb_tcp_print dispatches on the command, so a real command code (SMB2 NEGOTIATE = 0) is what buys depth.
554 (rtsp_print): An ASCII RTSP request or response with CRLF headers and a blank line: 'DESCRIBE rtsp://example.com/stream RTSP/1.0\r\nCSeq: 1\r\n\r\n'. rtsp_print is http_print's sibling and tokenises identically.
639 (msdp_print): type(1)=1 (Source-Active) length(2) then the SA entry of RP-address(4) prefix(4) mask-length(1); msdp_print switches on the type octet and 4 (SA-Request) is the other main branch.
646 (ldp_print): Exactly the port-646/UDP recipe: version(2)=1 pdu-length(2) ldp-identifier(6) then TLVs.
1723 (pptp_print): length(2) message-type(2)=1 (control) magic(4) = 'P' 'P' 'T' 'P' control-type(2)=1 (Start-Control-Connection-Request) reserved(2) protocol-version(2) then the SCCRQ body. The 4-octet 'PPTP' magic is verified first and a wrong magic stops the printer.
2049 (nfs_print (either end)): Exactly the port-2049/UDP recipe: the 4-octet record mark then a SUNRPC CALL with program 100003. On TCP the path is print-tcp.c:842-872, which additionally requires length >= 4, reads fraglen = GET_BE_U_4(bp) & 0x7FFFFFFF and clamps it to length - 4, then checks rm_direction (0 = CALL with dport 2049, 1 = REPLY with sport 2049).
6379 (redis_print): A RESP array: '*1\r\n$4\r\nPING\r\n'. resp_print walks the RESP framing, so the '*'/'$'/'+'/'-' type octets and the CRLF terminators are the structure it needs; '+OK\r\n' and '-ERR unknown\r\n' are its other branches.
6633 (openflow_print (old)): version(1)=1 (OF 1.0) type(1)=0 (HELLO) length(2)=8 xid(4). openflow_print switches on both version and type; version 4 type 0 is the modern equivalent and reaches the OF 1.3 parser.
6653 (openflow_print (IANA)): version(1)=4 type(1)=0 (HELLO) length(2)=8 xid(4); the IANA-assigned port uses the same header.
8080 (http_print (alt)): Identical to port 80; HTTP_PORT_ALT is the second demux entry for the same printer.
8554 (rtsp_print (alt)): Identical to port 554.
10288 (beep_print): An ASCII BEEP frame: '<greeting>\r\n' or 'MSG 0 0 . 0 0\r\nContent-Type: application/beep\r\n\r\npayload\r\n.END\r\n'. beep_print parses the profile and the frame header.
PCAPRECORD.AppData.algorithm: length = total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 - tcp_hdr_len*4 for TCP (line 162), or udp_hdr_len - 8 for UDP (line 170); emitted only when positive (lines 163, 171). Both expressions match the decoder's own arithmetic: print-tcp.c computes length the same way before the test at line 749, and print-udp.c:383-386 applies 'ulen -= sizeof(struct udphdr); length -= sizeof(struct udphdr); if (ulen < length) length = ulen;'.
PCAPRECORD.AppData.covers: Every octet of the IP datagram after the transport header, for TCP and UDP alike: the application message itself. It covers no header octets and no trailing Layer 2 Padding, and it is counted by total_length, by incl_len and, for UDP, additionally by udp_hdr_len.
PCAPRECORD.AppData.notes: This is the highest-value field in the template, and the .bt hides it under a generic name in two separate places. content_is_free is false here, unlike the other payload entries in this file, because for a demuxed port the message bytes ARE the structure that buys depth - there is no framing-versus-contents split to exploit. Three interactions matter. (1) The RST flag: print-tcp.c:764-770 returns for any segment with TH_RST set, under -nr merely TCHECKing the payload, so a TCP record that carries application data must not set RST or its AppData is wasted. (2) The port choice: Layer_4.SrcPort and Layer_4.DstPort are Tier B with a demux table, and the per-port recipe above is keyed off them, so the two must be chosen together. (3) tcp_hdr_len: an over-long TCP header consumes octets that would otherwise be payload, so a record aiming at deep application-layer coverage should use tcp_hdr_len 5 unless the TCP options themselves are the target. The two instantiations at lines 165 and 173 are mutually exclusive per record - a datagram is either TCP or UDP - so this one entry covers both and the generator selects the branch from Layer_3.L4proto.

PCAPRECORD.padding.tier_rationale: Its length is the expression incl_len - len_before_l3 - total_length at line 177, and if those three disagree the record ends at the wrong file offset: the next PCAPRECORD header is read from the middle of a frame, so libpcap's pcap_next_packet either reports a short/truncated record against EOF or hands tcpdump four nonsense length words and every subsequent record is garbage. That is the Tier A test met literally - the decoder stops doing useful work. The octets themselves are inspected by nothing: tcpdump has no notion of Ethernet pad bytes and they fall outside total_length, so their CONTENT is free and the AMOUNT is a free choice made through incl_len, which is where the diversity lives.
PCAPRECORD.padding.description: Trailing octets appended so the frame reaches a claimed size, present only when incl_len exceeds len_before_l3 + total_length; models both Ethernet minimum-frame padding and a capture that recorded more than the datagram claims.
PCAPRECORD.padding.algorithm: length = incl_len - len_before_l3 - total_length, emitted only when that difference is positive (line 176's guard). len_before_l3 is 0, 14 or 18 as described under PCAPRECORD.incl_len. The natural non-zero choice is the amount needed to reach the 60-octet IEEE 802.3 minimum frame size (64 with the FCS, which a pcap file never contains): padding_len = max(0, 60 - len_before_l3 - total_length). Any smaller positive value is equally accepted by the decoder.
PCAPRECORD.padding.covers: The octets between the end of the IP datagram and the end of the captured frame body. It is counted by incl_len and is NOT counted by total_length, which is precisely what makes it distinguishable from application data.
PCAPRECORD.padding.notes: Real Ethernet pads with zeros and zero is the value to prefer, but no decoder checks. This array is the only way the template can make incl_len differ from len_before_l3 + total_length, so it is the mechanism behind the 'capture longer than the datagram claims' case; combined with a deliberately small total_length it exercises print-ip.c:347's "[total length %u > length %u]" warning from the opposite direction. The natural non-zero amount is what IEEE 802.3 needs to reach the 60-octet minimum frame size (64 with the FCS, which a pcap file never contains). Emitting padding_len = 0 for most records keeps the file small and is the common real-world case. Tier close call: this entry was first recorded as Tier B on the grounds that the amount of padding is a free enumerated choice; it is Tier A because checklist item 2 puts every length field there and because the length, unlike the amount, is not free at all - it is whatever incl_len minus the frame body works out to. The freedom is real and is recorded on PCAPRECORD.incl_len (Tier A calculated_value, listed in diversity_axes with must_remain_unconstrained true) rather than here.
