Line 462 gates the relative-sequence hash lookup and the 'ack' text on ACK. Line 470 gates 'urg' on URG. Lines 765-771 return early for RST, skipping the port demux entirely. Lines 489-742 walk the options, with a distinct case per kind and a shared 'bad' exit at line 876 for any inconsistent length byte.

diversity_axes.axis: record repetition count - how many PCAPRECORD structs the while(!FEof()) loop at lines 217-220 emits per output file
diversity_axes.why: This is the template's only repeat-controlling construct and it is not a field, so it cannot be constrained by narrowing anything: the loop runs to end of file and the file's length is whatever the generator wrote. The count is set as the output_budget on the 'PCAPRECORD stream' entry in structure, and no field was capped to achieve it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each record is an independent pass through pcap_next_packet (sf-pcap.c:492) and then through the whole link-layer and protocol printer stack, so more records means more distinct paths per file. The count also bounds the damage from a desynchronised incl_len: once one record's length is wrong, every record after it is lost, so a moderate count with correct lengths beats a large count with one bad record.

diversity_axes.axis: IPv4 datagram size, which sets the size of Layer_4.packet, of PCAPRECORD.AppData for TCP, and through incl_len of the whole record
diversity_axes.why: It is the budget every payload is derived from, so it must vary across files - but it must vary by deriving the payload from it, never by shrinking it to fit a precomputed payload. That is the PNG-versus-GIF distinction: a fixed set of datagram sizes would collapse the record-size distribution and with it the padding, truncation and caplen branches.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-ip.c:346-350 compares it against the captured length and prints "[total length %u > length %u]" on overrun. It is the argument to ip_demux_print at line 494 as ND_MIN(length - hlen, len), so it directly bounds how many octets every transport and application printer is allowed to walk. print-tcp.c:759-763 and print-udp.c:380-385 both re-derive the payload length from it.

diversity_axes.axis: TCP header length in 32-bit words: 5 (no options) through 15, which trades option-walk coverage against application-payload coverage
diversity_axes.why: It is the multiplier in both line 110's Crap[tcp_hdr_len*4-13] and line 162's AppDataLen, so within a fixed total_length it moves octets between the options area and the payload. Varying it opens print-tcp.c's per-option switch at 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 words and closes it again at 5, and both ends are worth hitting.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-tcp.c:489-742 walks the options only when the header is longer than 20 octets, with a case per kind and the shared LENCHECK/​'bad' exit. Line 754 recomputes header_len = TH_OFF(tp) * 4 and line 759-763 aborts the record if the captured frame is shorter than that. print-ip.c:344 applies the analogous check to the IP header length.

diversity_axes.axis: UDP datagram length, which alone sets the size of PCAPRECORD.AppData for UDP
diversity_axes.why: Line 170 sizes AppData as udp_hdr_len - 8 and total_length does not appear in that expression, so this field is the UDP equivalent of total_length for payload purposes. It must be free to vary, and the AppData length must be derived from it rather than the reverse.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-udp.c:380-381 rejects a value below 8 with ND_ICHECKMSG_ZU("undersized-udplength", ...); lines 382-385 subtract the header and clamp the dissected length to min(ulen - 8, length - 8), which is what decides whether a demuxed printer receives any octets at all. A value of exactly 8 hands every printer an empty payload.

diversity_axes.axis: captured frame length, which fixes the record boundary and the padding length
diversity_axes.why: It is the offset of the next record, so it is simultaneously the strictest derived value in the file and the field whose variation across records produces the file's size distribution. Nothing about it should be ranged: it is computed as len_before_l3 + total_length + padding, and it is the padding term - not incl_len - that absorbs any intended frame-size variation.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: sf-pcap.c:589-608 rejects a value above MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN (262144) for the whole file; sf-pcap.c:611-712 truncates to p->snapshot when it exceeds snaplen; sf-pcap.c:744-752 reads exactly caplen octets and reports 'truncated dump file' if the file ends first. Every one of those is a distinct branch, and reaching the truncation branches at all requires incl_len to vary against snaplen.

diversity_axes.axis: IP header length in 32-bit words - listed here because it appears in payload_wellformedness.derives_from, but it is NOT an available axis in this template
diversity_axes.why: must_remain_unconstrained is false for this one field, and the reason is the template rather than the format. Lines 75-84 emit a fixed 20-octet IPv4 header with no options array - the only array sized from hdr_length, Unknown[hdr_length-4] at line 87, sits in the else branch for proto_type != 0x0800 and that branch cannot complete a record, because line 158 then dereferences an undeclared L3.L4proto. So every octet-count expression that multiplies ip_hdr_len by 4 (lines 93, 114, 162) agrees with the bytes on disk only when ip_hdr_len is 5. Offering 6..15 would not add diversity, it would shift the transport header by 4 octets per extra word and mis-demux every port. This is a recorded deviation from the derives_from rule and is also noted in meta.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-ip.c:343-344 computes hlen = IP_HL(ip) * 4 and rejects anything below 20 octets with " [header length %u < 20]"; for 6..15 it walks the options, but only under -v, and under 'tcpdump -nr' the value merely relocates the transport header.

diversity_axes.axis: declared snapshot length: 0 (which libpcap substitutes with the DLT maximum), the true maximum incl_len, or a value below it to provoke truncation
diversity_axes.why: It is a file-wide bound on every record and it is not encoded per record, so it costs nothing to vary between files. Two of the three settings are behaviourally identical - 0 and the true maximum both deliver every octet - while a value below the largest incl_len opens libpcap's truncation path, which is code no correctly-sized file reaches.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: savefile.c's pcapint_adjust_snapshot substitutes max_snaplen_for_dlt(linktype) for 0 and for anything above INT_MAX, so both are safe. sf-pcap.c:611-712 then compares each caplen against p->snapshot, reads only p->snapshot octets at line 661, sets bytes_to_discard at 685 and clamps hdr->caplen at 712. sf-pcap.c:589-608 is the separate hard-error path for caplen above MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN.

diversity_axes.axis: savefile minor version 0..4, which selects how libpcap interprets the incl_len/orig_len pair
diversity_axes.why: All five values are accepted and each is a distinct branch of the lengths_swapped switch, so this is free diversity - with one coupling the generator must respect. Under 0, 1 and 2 libpcap exchanges caplen and len after reading them, which means the record header must be written in the pre-2.3 order (orig_len before incl_len) for the file to stay coherent. Version 3 exchanges them only when the first exceeds the second. Version 4 is the plain order.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: sf-pcap.c:286-294 admits version_minor <= PCAP_VERSION_MINOR (4, pcap.h:147) with version_major 2, plus the DG/UX pair 543.0. sf-pcap.c:389-406 maps the minor version to SWAPPED / MAYBE_SWAPPED / NOT_SWAPPED, and sf-pcap.c:564-583 applies it per record.

diversity_axes.axis: the six octets of each of Layer_2.DstMac and Layer_2.SrcMac - two independent 48-bit words per Ethernet frame
diversity_axes.why: Nothing validates a MAC address anywhere in the pipeline, so all 2^48 values per address are processed identically and pinning them would remove two full diversity words per frame for no depth at all. The I/G and U/L bits, broadcast and locally-administered addresses are all equally legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-ether.c formats the addresses with mac48_string() and prints them only under -e; without -e it TCHECKs the 14 octets and dispatches on the EtherType. No branch anywhere depends on the address content, which is exactly why the field is Tier C.

diversity_axes.axis: the four octets of each of Layer_3.SRC_IP and Layer_3.DST_IP - two independent 32-bit words per datagram
diversity_axes.why: Address content never gates dissection, so both words are free. They do reach the relative-sequence hash in tcp_print, keyed on source, destination and port, so varying them also varies which hash bucket a TCP record lands in and whether the 'ack' text is relative or absolute.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-ip.c:473-477 prints 'src > dst:' for non-TCP/UDP/SCTP/DCCP protocols, using GET_IPADDR_STRING. print-tcp.c keys its tcp_seq_hash on the address pair. Multicast, loopback, link-local and 0.0.0.0 are all accepted; no printer branches on the value beyond formatting it.

diversity_axes.axis: the 16-bit IP identification word
diversity_axes.why: Never examined under 'tcpdump -nr' - it is printed only inside the ndo_vflag block at print-ip.c:414-419 - so all 65536 values are free. The one caveat is coupling with fragmentation: when the MF bit or a non-zero offset is in use, the identification word keys tcpdump's fragment reporting, so records that are meant to look like parts of one datagram must share it and unrelated fragments must not.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-ip.c:414-419 prints 'id %u, offset %u, flags [%s]' under -v. No other code path reads it.

diversity_axes.axis: the IPv4 time-to-live octet, 0..255
diversity_axes.why: No decoder branch depends on it under 'tcpdump -nr'; it is printed as a bare number at print-ip.c:413 inside the verbose block and is never interpreted. Its only soft association is convention - OSPF and VRRP use 255, BGP uses 1 or 255 - and those are cosmetic.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-ip.c:413 prints it under -v. Nothing else reads it.

diversity_axes.axis: the IPv4 DSCP/ECN octet, 0..255
diversity_axes.why: Free for the same reason as TTL: print-ip.c reads it only for verbose output and no printer branches on the value. All 256 settings produce a parseable file.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Printed under -v as the TOS/DSCP value. No dissection branch keys on it.

diversity_axes.axis: the 32-bit TCP initial sequence number
diversity_axes.why: Every value is legal and the field is never validated. It does participate in coverage indirectly: print-tcp.c:462 looks up a relative-sequence hash keyed on the connection tuple, and whether SEQ is printed as relative or absolute depends on that lookup, so a wide spread of values is what makes both renderings appear.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-tcp.c:462-470 reads it for the relative-sequence computation and prints 'seq' only when SYN, FIN or RST is set, or under -v. Lines 765-771 return early for RST after printing it.

diversity_axes.axis: the 32-bit TCP acknowledgement number
diversity_axes.why: Free like SEQ, and equally involved in the flag-gated printing paths. Varying it against SEQ is what produces the distinct relative/absolute rendering outcomes.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-tcp.c:462 gates the 'ack %u' text and the relative-sequence hash on the ACK flag in Layer_4.Crap, not on this value, so the value itself is unconstrained by any branch.

diversity_axes.axis: the record's seconds timestamp, a full 32-bit word
diversity_axes.why: Unconstrained in value - libpcap never validates it - but it is the field whose width must stay exact. The .bt declares it time_t at line 137 while the classic savefile format fixes it at 4 octets, and a generator that writes it as 8 shifts the other three record-header fields and desynchronises every record that follows. The axis here is the timestamp value, and the width is a hard structural pin.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: sf-pcap.c reads it into hdr->ts.tv_sec via the same 4-octet read as the other three fields. pcap_dump writes 4 octets. Timestamp ordering across records is not required and is never checked.

diversity_axes.axis: the record's microsecond component, 0..999999 in ordinary files
diversity_axes.why: Value-free for the decoder: nothing validates the range. Values above 999999 are still parsed and simply print as a large fractional part, so the full 32-bit word is usable if the generator wants to probe that.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Read into hdr->ts.tv_usec alongside ts_sec at sf-pcap.c's record-header read. No branch depends on it.

diversity_axes.axis: the 12-bit VLAN identifier, 0..4095, alongside the 3-bit priority and 1-bit dei packed into the same uint16
diversity_axes.why: Printed but never branched on, so all 4096 identifiers are free and the priority and dei bit-fields with them. The tag's mere presence already bought the 802.1Q printer via the Layer_2.L3type axis; these values add variation inside it at no cost.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The 802.1Q handler reads the packed octet pair and prints the VLAN id, priority and DEI, then dispatches on the inner EtherType. Only Dot1q.L3type is constrained, to 0x0800, because line 155 feeds it to Layer_3 as proto_type.

diversity_axes.axis: the on-the-wire length as originally captured, paired with incl_len
diversity_axes.why: The relationship orig_len >= incl_len is what a real capture writes, and libpcap only ever uses the inequality as a hint. Keeping it derived from the frame preserves the realistic distribution; deliberately inverting it is a separate probe that version_minor 0..3 turns into a length swap, so the two axes are coupled and should be varied together.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: sf-pcap.c:564-583 may exchange caplen and len depending on version_minor, then sf-pcap.c:611-712 uses the resulting caplen for truncation. hdr->len itself is passed to the printer and printed as the frame length under -v; nothing rejects len < caplen.

diversity_axes.axis: the 4 reserved bits sharing the octet with tcp_hdr_len
diversity_axes.why: Set bits are ignored by every printer, so the 16 combinations are free. The octet is shared with tcp_hdr_len's high nibble, which is why this axis is listed as bits rather than as an independent word.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: print-tcp.c reads TH_OFF(tp) from the same octet and never inspects the reserved nibble.

payload_wellformedness.codec: TCP fixed header tail (7 octets) followed by the RFC 793 / RFC 6691 option TLV stream: kind(1) [length(1) value(length-2)], where kinds 0 (EOL) and 1 (NOP) are zero-length and carry no length octet (print-tcp.c:100 '#define ZEROLENOPT(o) ((o) == TCPOPT_EOL || (o) == TCPOPT_NOP)').
payload_wellformedness.must_produce: Octet layout of Crap, indexed from 0: Crap[0] = control flags (FIN 0x01, SYN 0x02, RST 0x04, PSH 0x08, ACK 0x10, URG 0x20, ECE 0x40, CWR 0x80); Crap[1..2] = window size, big-endian; Crap[3..4] = checksum, big-endian; Crap[5..6] = urgent pointer, big-endian; Crap[7..] = the options area, exactly (tcp_hdr_len - 5) * 4 octets when tcp_hdr_len > 5. The options area must be a sequence of well-formed TLVs padded to a 4-octet multiple with kind 0 (EOL) or kind 1 (NOP), each TLV's length byte >= 2, <= the octets remaining in the area, and >= 2 + the kind-specific datalen print-tcp.c checks. Legal kinds and required total lengths: 0 EOL (1 octet, terminates the loop), 1 NOP (1), 2 MSS (4: kind len 02 02 mss-hi mss-lo), 3 window scale (3), 4 SACK-permitted (2), 5 SACK (2 + 8n; datalen % 8 != 0 makes print-tcp.c:524 print " invalid sack"), 6 ECHO (6), 7 ECHOREPLY (6), 8 timestamps (10: kind len 0A TSval(4) TSecr(4)), 11 CC (6), 12 CCNEW (6), 13 CCECHO (6), 19 MD5 signature (18), 20 SCPS (4), 28 user timeout (4), 29 TCP-AO (>= 4), 30 MPTCP (>= 4), 34 TCP Fast Open (6 or 10, i.e. a 4- or 8-octet cookie), 254 experimental (>= 4, with the leading 2-octet magic 0xF989 selecting the TFO sub-parser). Any other kind prints as 'unknown-%u' from tok2str at line 507 and is still accepted provided its length byte is consistent.
payload_wellformedness.decoder_gate: A length byte below 2 or above the remaining header length, or a kind whose datalen overruns it, sends print-tcp.c to 'bad' at line 876: it prints "[bad opt]", closes any open bracket and returns. Nothing downstream runs - no ", length N", no port demux, no ftp_print/http_print/domain_print/bgp_print. A length byte of 2 for a kind that needs more (MSS, timestamps) also trips LENCHECK. Random bytes therefore lose the entire TCP application layer for that record.

payload_wellformedness.codec: protocol-selected, chosen by Layer_3.L4proto through tcpdump's ip_demux_print(). The named-printer set reachable with Layer_3.version pinned to 4 is protocol numbers 1 (ICMP), 2 (IGMP), 4 (IP-in-IP), 8 (EGP), 9 (IGRP), 33 (DCCP), 46 (RSVP), 47 (GRE), 50 (ESP), 51 (AH), 54 (NHRP), 55 (MOBILE), 88 (EIGRP), 89 (OSPF), 103 (PIM), 108 (IPComp), 112 (VRRP), 113 (PGM) and 132 (SCTP). Numbers 58 (ICMPv6) and 143 (Ethernet) are IPv6-only: with version 4 they print "[ICMPv6 requires IPv6]" and "[ethernet requires IPv6]" (print-ip-demux.c:59-62, 161-166). Number 77 (ND) prints only " nd %u" and 59 (NONE) only "no next header"; every remaining number reaches the default branch at lines 225-231, which prints the protocol name and the length and never reads a byte.
payload_wellformedness.must_produce: For one of the named-printer protocol numbers, a complete minimum message for that protocol with every internal length, count and magic consistent. For any other number, arbitrary octets - nothing reads them. In all cases the octet count must be exactly total_length - ip_hdr_len*4, and total_length must in turn agree with incl_len and the octets actually present.
payload_wellformedness.decoder_gate: A wrong protocol number is not a rejection at all: the default branch prints the name and length and stops, which is a shallow but perfectly legal outcome. For a named number with random bytes the printer's own header check fires - icmp_print '[|icmp]', sctp_print '[bad chunk length]', ospf_print '[ospf: truncated]', bgp-less PIM/IGMP similar - and the body never runs. The length gate is the harder one: a packet[] shorter than total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 desynchronises the record and libpcap aborts the rest of the file.

payload_wellformedness.codec: port-selected application protocol rather than a single codec. On the UDP side tcpdump's udp_print demuxes 68 ports to named printers (domain_print for DNS and mDNS, bootp_print for DHCP, ntp_print, snmp_print's BER/ASN.1 walker, rip_print, isakmp_print, vxlan_print and geneve_print which recurse into a nested Ethernet frame, radius_print, sip_print, dhcp6_print, l2tp_print, bfd_print, sflow_print, babel_print and others). On the TCP side tcp_print demuxes 22 ports to ftp_print, ssh_print, telnet_print, smtp_print, whois_print, domain_print, http_print, netbios_ssn_print, bgp_print, rpki_rtr_print, smb_tcp_print, rtsp_print, msdp_print, ldp_print, pptp_print, nfs_print, resp_print, openflow_print and beep_print. For every other port the payload is unstructured and free.
payload_wellformedness.must_produce: For a demuxed port, a complete minimum message for that protocol, including every internal length, count and magic that the protocol's own printer checks. For any other port, arbitrary octets. In both cases the octet count must equal what the enclosing length field claims: for TCP, AppDataLen = total_length - ip_hdr_len*4 - tcp_hdr_len*4 (line 162); for UDP, AppDataLen = udp_hdr_len - 8 (line 170).
payload_wellformedness.decoder_gate: Zero length: print-tcp.c:749 returns before the demux, so the whole TCP application layer is skipped; print-udp.c:385 clamps length to ulen - 8, so the UDP demux printers receive zero octets and each bails at its own header check. Random bytes with a non-zero length: the correct printer is still selected by port, but it fails its first structural test and prints one bracketed complaint - domain_print '[|domain]', http_print nothing at all, ssh_print nothing, bgp_print '[BGP: Message length %u is less than the minimum header length %u]', snmp_print '[snmp: truncated]', openflow_print '[openflow] (invalid)'. The named printer's body is then never executed, which is exactly the coverage this field buys.
